speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Home Affairs (Ms Sun Xueling) (for the Minister for Home Affairs)
text: Firefighters took 60 hours to extinguish the fire.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Home Affairs (Ms Sun Xueling) (for the Minister for Home Affairs)
text: More recently, on 15 April 2019, a fire broke out at the Notre Dame cathedral and spread rapidly.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Home Affairs (Ms Sun Xueling) (for the Minister for Home Affairs)
text: The fire was put out only after three hours of intense firefighting.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Home Affairs (Ms Sun Xueling) (for the Minister for Home Affairs)
text: While the structure was saved, the cathedral’s spire and most of its roof were destroyed and its upper walls severely damaged.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Home Affairs (Ms Sun Xueling) (for the Minister for Home Affairs)
text: Investigations are still ongoing, but it is already evident that the cathedral lacked fundamental fire-prevention safeguards, such as firewalls and sprinkler systems.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Home Affairs (Ms Sun Xueling) (for the Minister for Home Affairs)
text: Some of these safeguards were deliberately omitted due to design considerations and these regulatory decisions are now being called into question in the aftermath of this tragic loss.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Home Affairs (Ms Sun Xueling) (for the Minister for Home Affairs)
text: These devastating incidents remind us of the catastrophic damage that can be caused by fires and the importance of strong regulatory regimes to prevent such tragedies in the first place.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Home Affairs (Ms Sun Xueling) (for the Minister for Home Affairs)
text: In comparison, New York’s fire fatality rate was 15 times higher in 2018 and Tokyo’s was nine times higher.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Home Affairs (Ms Sun Xueling) (for the Minister for Home Affairs)
text: That said, we should not be complacent and think we are immune.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Home Affairs (Ms Sun Xueling) (for the Minister for Home Affairs)
text: We would do well to remember the recent blaze at Jalan Buroh, where a fire engulfed a liquid petroleum gas facility about the size of two football fields.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Home Affairs (Ms Sun Xueling) (for the Minister for Home Affairs)
text: One worker perished and two others were hospitalised for burn injuries.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Home Affairs (Ms Sun Xueling) (for the Minister for Home Affairs)
text: The fire also caused significant damage to property.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Home Affairs (Ms Sun Xueling) (for the Minister for Home Affairs)
text: In fact, it could have been worse, given the large amounts of liquid petroleum gas nearby and if not for the valiant response by our SCDF firefighters.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Home Affairs (Ms Sun Xueling) (for the Minister for Home Affairs)
text: Our fire safety regulatory regime plays an important role in preventing fires and mitigating their impact.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Home Affairs (Ms Sun Xueling) (for the Minister for Home Affairs)
text: The Fire Safety Act sets out general provisions related to fire safety, such as various regulatory requirements and the responsibilities of relevant parties, including industry professionals and building owners.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Home Affairs (Ms Sun Xueling) (for the Minister for Home Affairs)
text: There is also a Code of Practice for Fire Precautions in Buildings, simply known as the "Fire Code", which sets out specific fire safety standards that must be complied with when a building is being constructed or when it undergoes addition and alteration (A&A) works.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Home Affairs (Ms Sun Xueling) (for the Minister for Home Affairs)
text: The Singapore Civil Defence Force (SCDF) regularly updates the Fire Code.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Home Affairs (Ms Sun Xueling) (for the Minister for Home Affairs)
text: It was most recently updated in May this year.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Home Affairs (Ms Sun Xueling) (for the Minister for Home Affairs)
text: The Fire Safety Act, on the other hand, was last amended in 2016.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Home Affairs (Ms Sun Xueling) (for the Minister for Home Affairs)
text: It is timely for us to review the Act again.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Home Affairs (Ms Sun Xueling) (for the Minister for Home Affairs)
text: I will start with our proposal to enhance the fire safety of buildings in Singapore.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Home Affairs (Ms Sun Xueling) (for the Minister for Home Affairs)
text: Currently, SCDF requires new buildings and buildings undergoing A&A works to conform to the prevailing Fire Code.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Home Affairs (Ms Sun Xueling) (for the Minister for Home Affairs)
text: However, older buildings that have not undergone A&A works are not subject to the latest requirements.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Home Affairs (Ms Sun Xueling) (for the Minister for Home Affairs)
text: Many, therefore, have not upgraded their fire safety measures for a long time.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Home Affairs (Ms Sun Xueling) (for the Minister for Home Affairs)
text: On top of that, some have occupants with reduced mobility, such as the elderly and patients.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Home Affairs (Ms Sun Xueling) (for the Minister for Home Affairs)
text: While these buildings have some measures which provide baseline fire safety, overall, they have a higher fire risk profile.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Home Affairs (Ms Sun Xueling) (for the Minister for Home Affairs)
text: The safety of the occupants and the public who visit such buildings can be enhanced by installing selected upgrades.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Home Affairs (Ms Sun Xueling) (for the Minister for Home Affairs)
text: SCDF needs to be given these powers to direct such upgrades.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Home Affairs (Ms Sun Xueling) (for the Minister for Home Affairs)
text: To achieve this, clause 10 repeals and re-enacts section 20 and inserts a new section 20A, which will empower the Commissioner of Civil Defence to issue an order to require building owners to install fire safety measures, if these measures are assessed to be necessary for public safety.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Home Affairs (Ms Sun Xueling) (for the Minister for Home Affairs)
text: SCDF is keenly aware that this will impose additional costs on building owners.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Home Affairs (Ms Sun Xueling) (for the Minister for Home Affairs)
text: In exercising this power, SCDF will be judicious and will take a risk-based approach in identifying buildings and the fire safety upgrades that will be required of them.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Home Affairs (Ms Sun Xueling) (for the Minister for Home Affairs)
text: For now, we have identified around 500 buildings.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Home Affairs (Ms Sun Xueling) (for the Minister for Home Affairs)
text: These are mostly commercial, industrial and Government buildings, based on factors, such as the age of the buildings and the profile of the occupants.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Home Affairs (Ms Sun Xueling) (for the Minister for Home Affairs)
text: One example is Ling Kwang Home, which houses elderly residents.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Home Affairs (Ms Sun Xueling) (for the Minister for Home Affairs)
text: The Home was built in 1983, in compliance with the 1982 Fire Code.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Home Affairs (Ms Sun Xueling) (for the Minister for Home Affairs)
text: Since then, newer versions of the Fire Code have introduced additional provisions for healthcare facilities, such as the requirement to have at least two areas of refuge on each floor to facilitate fire evacuation.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Home Affairs (Ms Sun Xueling) (for the Minister for Home Affairs)
text: But as the Home has not undergone A&A works, it has not been subject to these new requirements.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Home Affairs (Ms Sun Xueling) (for the Minister for Home Affairs)
text: For the sake of its residents, the fire safety measures of the Home should be upgraded.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Home Affairs (Ms Sun Xueling) (for the Minister for Home Affairs)
text: SCDF has worked with the Home to identify the critical measures required and I am pleased to share that the Home has voluntarily commenced works, even though the Bill has not been passed yet.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Home Affairs (Ms Sun Xueling) (for the Minister for Home Affairs)
text: Building owners who encounter practical difficulties may approach SCDF to explore options and SCDF may provide flexibility on a case-by-case basis.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Home Affairs (Ms Sun Xueling) (for the Minister for Home Affairs)
text: We will also provide an avenue for appeal.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Home Affairs (Ms Sun Xueling) (for the Minister for Home Affairs)
text: In May 2017, a fire occurred at an industrial building along Toh Guan Road, which resulted in one fatality.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Home Affairs (Ms Sun Xueling) (for the Minister for Home Affairs)
text: SCDF then undertook a comprehensive verification of the fire safety of buildings that could potentially have used similar cladding and found other lapses.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Home Affairs (Ms Sun Xueling) (for the Minister for Home Affairs)
text: We then convened a cladding review panel, which proposed various measures to tighten control over the supply chain.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Home Affairs (Ms Sun Xueling) (for the Minister for Home Affairs)
text: The parties involved in the supply chain for fire safety products include: (a) manufacturers and suppliers; (b) laboratories that test the fire safety performance of the products and issue test reports; (c) certification bodies that review the test reports and issue Certificates of Conformity (CoC) that certify the fire safety performance of the products; and (d) installers of these products.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Home Affairs (Ms Sun Xueling) (for the Minister for Home Affairs)
text: These supply chain actors all have a part to play in making sure that only products and materials that meet SCDF’s prescribed standards in the Fire Code are used for our buildings.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Home Affairs (Ms Sun Xueling) (for the Minister for Home Affairs)
text: However, under the current Fire Safety Act, SCDF can only take limited enforcement actions against some of the parties, for example: (a) the owners and occupiers for failing to appoint an appropriate Qualified Person or Fire Safety Engineer to prepare the required plans and supervise fire safety works; (b) any person who commences or carries out or authorises the commencement or carrying out of fire safety works without the approval of Commissioner, or without the supervision of an appropriate Qualified Person or Fire Safety Engineer; and (c) Qualified Persons, Fire Safety Engineers and Registered Inspectors who do not carry out their responsibilities in ensuring that the fire safety works are in accordance with the Act requirements.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Home Affairs (Ms Sun Xueling) (for the Minister for Home Affairs)
text: We cannot prosecute other parties involved in the supply chain, nor can we issue rectification orders, even if the product has been found to be non-compliant.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Home Affairs (Ms Sun Xueling) (for the Minister for Home Affairs)
text: For example, under the current Act, SCDF is unable to take action against: (a) the manufacturers and suppliers; (b) the test laboratories that issue a false test report; and (c) the certification bodies that issue a CoC that falsely represents that the product meets the required standards.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Home Affairs (Ms Sun Xueling) (for the Minister for Home Affairs)
text: In addition, there may be situations where SCDF reasonably suspects certain products or materials to be non-compliant with the required standards.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Home Affairs (Ms Sun Xueling) (for the Minister for Home Affairs)
text: However, SCDF currently only has the power to order building owners to test the products, whereas there are instances where the culpability may lie with the certification body or the CoC holder.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Home Affairs (Ms Sun Xueling) (for the Minister for Home Affairs)
text: The new section 33 will, therefore, empower the Commissioner to require a certification body or a CoC holder to test any fire safety product, including installed products.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Home Affairs (Ms Sun Xueling) (for the Minister for Home Affairs)
text: In addition, if the Commissioner has reason to believe that any person is supplying or offering to supply non-compliant fire safety products despite knowing that they are non-compliant, or falsely representing these products to be compliant, he can order the certification body not to issue any more CoCs to this person, including for other products.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Home Affairs (Ms Sun Xueling) (for the Minister for Home Affairs)
text: If the certification body does not comply with SCDF’s orders, the Minister may gazette these products as non-compliant.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Home Affairs (Ms Sun Xueling) (for the Minister for Home Affairs)
text: These new powers, Mr Speaker, will allow SCDF to deem products which SCDF reasonably suspects to have fire safety risks, to be non-compliant, thereby allowing SCDF to use its enforcement levers.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Home Affairs (Ms Sun Xueling) (for the Minister for Home Affairs)
text: I will now talk about SCDF’s investigative and enforcement powers.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Home Affairs (Ms Sun Xueling) (for the Minister for Home Affairs)
text: Apart from non-compliant fire safety products and materials, fire hazards also pose significant risks to public safety.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Home Affairs (Ms Sun Xueling) (for the Minister for Home Affairs)
text: Examples of fire hazards include overcrowding, non-maintenance of fire safety measures and obstruction of fire escape routes.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Home Affairs (Ms Sun Xueling) (for the Minister for Home Affairs)
text: They materially increase the likelihood of fires and the dangers when fires break out.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Home Affairs (Ms Sun Xueling) (for the Minister for Home Affairs)
text: Currently, when dealing with fire hazards, SCDF must first issue a Fire Hazard Abatement Notice and can only take action against the errant parties if they fail to comply with the Notice.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Home Affairs (Ms Sun Xueling) (for the Minister for Home Affairs)
text: Given that some fire hazards may pose serious fire safety risks, clause 9 inserts two new sections.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Home Affairs (Ms Sun Xueling) (for the Minister for Home Affairs)
text: This thus provides SCDF with an additional option of taking immediate prosecutorial action against those responsible for serious fire hazards, rather than being able to only issue a Fire Hazard Abatement Notice.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Home Affairs (Ms Sun Xueling) (for the Minister for Home Affairs)
text: Next, SCDF currently has some powers under the Fire Safety Act to enter premises linked to offences under the Act, to conduct investigations.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Home Affairs (Ms Sun Xueling) (for the Minister for Home Affairs)
text: However, this is not the full suite of powers needed in an investigation.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Home Affairs (Ms Sun Xueling) (for the Minister for Home Affairs)
text: SCDF has to work with the Police to conduct certain tasks, such as to take statements from relevant parties.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Home Affairs (Ms Sun Xueling) (for the Minister for Home Affairs)
text: We will empower SCDF to be able to pursue investigations independently, so as to expedite the investigation process.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Home Affairs (Ms Sun Xueling) (for the Minister for Home Affairs)
text: In addition, clause 6 amends section 8 to empower SCDF to enter any premises to obtain evidence related to the breach of a licensing condition by an alarm monitoring services licensee or to the commission of any offence under the Act.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Home Affairs (Ms Sun Xueling) (for the Minister for Home Affairs)
text: SCDF is the subject matter expert on fire investigations and these amendments will facilitate their investigations under the Act.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Home Affairs (Ms Sun Xueling) (for the Minister for Home Affairs)
text: The Bill also proposes to increase the penalties for five serious offences under the Fire Safety Act.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Home Affairs (Ms Sun Xueling) (for the Minister for Home Affairs)
text: These are: (a) unauthorised change of use of premises which may then render existing fire safety measures in the building to become inadequate; (b) failure of the Fire Safety Engineer to ensure that the engineering solution proposed for the building satisfies fire safety performance requirements; (c) failure of appointed Qualified Persons to supervise fire safety works; (d) failure of appointed Qualified Persons to submit relevant reports and certificates; and (e) failure of the appointed Registered Inspector to inspect and or verify that fire safety works have been completed according to approved plans.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Home Affairs (Ms Sun Xueling) (for the Minister for Home Affairs)
text: The enhanced penalties will be aligned with similar offences under the Fire Safety Act as well as other Acts, such as the Building Control Act and the Planning Act.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Home Affairs (Ms Sun Xueling) (for the Minister for Home Affairs)
text: This was benchmarked to a similar offence of an appointed accredited checker who fails to check detailed structural plans and to verify design calculations under the Building Control Act.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Home Affairs (Ms Sun Xueling) (for the Minister for Home Affairs)
text: I will now explain the fourth set of proposals that will optimise SCDF's capabilities and resources by allowing them to focus on complex areas which pose higher fire safety risks and outsource more routine and straightforward functions.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Home Affairs (Ms Sun Xueling) (for the Minister for Home Affairs)
text: SCDF conducts fire safety enforcement inspections of buildings.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Home Affairs (Ms Sun Xueling) (for the Minister for Home Affairs)
text: These can be categorised into scheduled and non-scheduled inspections.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Home Affairs (Ms Sun Xueling) (for the Minister for Home Affairs)
text: The fire stations send their officers to conduct scheduled inspections of premises within their jurisdiction, in order to allow the officers to familiarise themselves with the buildings and provide them with an opportunity to engage the owners and occupiers.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Home Affairs (Ms Sun Xueling) (for the Minister for Home Affairs)
text: On the other hand, non-scheduled inspections arise from ad hoc feedback.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Home Affairs (Ms Sun Xueling) (for the Minister for Home Affairs)
text: Around half involve offences that are straightforward and can be easily established through visual inspections.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Home Affairs (Ms Sun Xueling) (for the Minister for Home Affairs)
text: Examples include obstruction to fire exit staircases and non-maintenance of fire extinguishers.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Home Affairs (Ms Sun Xueling) (for the Minister for Home Affairs)
text: To enable our SCDF officers to focus on more complex enforcement inspections, clause 8 will allow SCDF to appoint suitably-trained individuals to conduct fire safety building inspections and to exercise certain enforcement powers, such as the issuance of Fire Hazard Abatement Notices, for simple and straightforward cases.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Home Affairs (Ms Sun Xueling) (for the Minister for Home Affairs)
text: These appointed officers will be deemed to be public servants for the purposes of the Penal Code in their exercise of these powers.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Home Affairs (Ms Sun Xueling) (for the Minister for Home Affairs)
text: SCDF will exercise careful discretion in the scope of work to be outsourced and retain control over all fire safety enforcement actions.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Home Affairs (Ms Sun Xueling) (for the Minister for Home Affairs)
text: SCDF will also implement safeguards, such as random audits, and require appointed officers to wear body-worn cameras when they carry out inspections.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Home Affairs (Ms Sun Xueling) (for the Minister for Home Affairs)
text: This will ensure that the appointed officers conduct their inspections professionally and minimise the risk of any abuse of authority.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Home Affairs (Ms Sun Xueling) (for the Minister for Home Affairs)
text: Next, SCDF relies on third-party fire alarm operators to monitor and verify alarms in higher-risk premises before deploying SCDF's resources.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Home Affairs (Ms Sun Xueling) (for the Minister for Home Affairs)
text: During the recent Jalan Buroh fire, the alarms at the premises detected the fire and immediately alerted both the fire alarm operator and SCDF.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Home Affairs (Ms Sun Xueling) (for the Minister for Home Affairs)
text: The fire alarm operator quickly confirmed the fire incident and SCDF then dispatched its resources.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Home Affairs (Ms Sun Xueling) (for the Minister for Home Affairs)
text: Lastly, I will cover proposals that will provide greater clarity to the industry on fire safety requirements.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Home Affairs (Ms Sun Xueling) (for the Minister for Home Affairs)
text: This will provide clarity and consistency for all emergency preparedness requirements.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Home Affairs (Ms Sun Xueling) (for the Minister for Home Affairs)
text: SCDF will provide a one-off notification to owners of buildings that have been newly-designated.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Home Affairs (Ms Sun Xueling) (for the Minister for Home Affairs)
text: In addition, clause 2 amends section 2 to revise the definition of certain terms.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Home Affairs (Ms Sun Xueling) (for the Minister for Home Affairs)
text: An electronic version of the Fire Code which is published on SCDF's website will enable faster updates and facilitate access to the latest Fire Code by the industry.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Home Affairs (Ms Sun Xueling) (for the Minister for Home Affairs)
text: The amendments I have spelt out are required to ensure that we continue to have an effective regime, thereby ensuring an even safer Singapore.

speaker: Mr Christopher de Souza (Holland-Bukit Timah)
text: Fire has the potential to harm many more people in addition to the one who started it.

speaker: Mr Christopher de Souza (Holland-Bukit Timah)
text: Persons in the adjacent unit to where the fire started may also have their property affected and their lives threatened.

speaker: Mr Christopher de Souza (Holland-Bukit Timah)
text: The blocking of the fire escape passageways affects the people who use that passageway, not just the family in front of which the items are placed.

speaker: Mr Christopher de Souza (Holland-Bukit Timah)
text: Fire safety is a team effort and this Bill strengthens that resolve.

speaker: Mr Christopher de Souza (Holland-Bukit Timah)
text: This means that people cannot take for granted that they will be served the notice to comply before getting charged with an offence.

speaker: Mr Christopher de Souza (Holland-Bukit Timah)
text: There is also increased punishment if a person continues to contravene the Act.

speaker: Mr Christopher de Souza (Holland-Bukit Timah)
text: For example, the new section 2(4), as amended by clause 2(j) of the Bill, makes it a continual non-compliance with the Act a separate offence.

speaker: Mr Christopher de Souza (Holland-Bukit Timah)
text: The new section 20A(3)(b) in clause 10 also provides for enhanced sentence for a continuing offence for non-compliance with an order to install fire safety measures.

speaker: Mr Christopher de Souza (Holland-Bukit Timah)
text: These measures increase the cost of non-compliance, ensuring that it is not more cost-effective to commit an offence than to comply with an order.

speaker: Mr Christopher de Souza (Holland-Bukit Timah)
text: If old building structures are required to comply with the new safety code, the measures are potentially extremely onerous, especially if a renovation was not planned.

speaker: Mr Christopher de Souza (Holland-Bukit Timah)
text: For instance, it was reported in Channel NewsAsia that International Plaza would need to have fire escape staircases leading to the outside of the building and Ling Kwang Home for Senior Citizens would require fire compartmentalisation to facilitate horizontal evacuation.

speaker: Mr Christopher de Souza (Holland-Bukit Timah)
text: Would the Minister elaborate on how the measures will be tailored to the need of the safety of the public in those buildings and how the owners will be assisted in complying with the measures imposed?

speaker: Mr Christopher de Souza (Holland-Bukit Timah)
text: This is ideal, as buildings can be multi-purpose, and focuses on the rationale behind the categorising of a building as a public building, that is, safety of	the	public.

speaker: Mr Christopher de Souza (Holland-Bukit Timah)
text: Will current	building	owners who are affected by the change of definition of "public building" be notified and advised on how to comply with the new requirements?

speaker: Mr Christopher de Souza (Holland-Bukit Timah)
text: Currently, places where people assemble for religious or educational	purposes are expressly excluded from the definition of "public building" in paragraph	(d)(i).

speaker: Mr Christopher de Souza (Holland-Bukit Timah)
text: By way	of	illustration,	under	what circumstances	would	a place	of	worship	or	school be considered a public building?

speaker: Mr Christopher de Souza (Holland-Bukit Timah)
text: Would the Minister	also elaborate on what would be considered a section of the public?

speaker: Mr Christopher de Souza (Holland-Bukit Timah)
text: Second, this Bill regulates more stringently the provision of fire safety devices and fire alarm monitoring services.

speaker: Mr Christopher de Souza (Holland-Bukit Timah)
text: The regulatory framework for fire safety devices is meant to ensure accountability.

speaker: Mr Christopher de Souza (Holland-Bukit Timah)
text: For instance, the compliant-fire-safety product needs to have a certificate which can only be validly issued to a Singapore Citizen, a domicile of Singapore or a body corporate incorporated in Singapore.

speaker: Mr Christopher de Souza (Holland-Bukit Timah)
text: This makes sure that the law can be actively enforced, deterring	opportunistic	merchants	who	may	prey	on unsuspecting customers by providing subpar products but escape from law enforcement by remaining outside Singapore.

speaker: Mr Christopher de Souza (Holland-Bukit Timah)
text: Furthermore, the new Part V in clause 26 of this Bill ensures that the whole certification, supply, installation and sales process meets the standards required.

speaker: Mr Christopher de Souza (Holland-Bukit Timah)
text: The new section 32 deals with false test reports used for certification.

speaker: Mr Christopher de Souza (Holland-Bukit Timah)
text: The new section 32A deals with giving false information to the accredited certification body.

speaker: Mr Christopher de Souza (Holland-Bukit Timah)
text: New section 32B ensures that certification process is only done by those authorised.

speaker: Mr Christopher de Souza (Holland-Bukit Timah)
text: And new section 32C regulates the supply of regulated fire products, ensuring that people do not advertise non-certified products as certified ones.

speaker: Mr Christopher de Souza (Holland-Bukit Timah)
text: New section 32D deals with installing an uncertified fire product as well as the manner in which a certified fire product is installed, making sure its quality is not compromised when it is being installed.

speaker: Mr Christopher de Souza (Holland-Bukit Timah)
text: Some offences, such as new section 32D(4), even have an enhanced offence with a jail term if harm to a person results because of that negligent or reckless act.

speaker: Mr Christopher de Souza (Holland-Bukit Timah)
text: While the specific standard of conduct is not found in the Bill, the Bill requires certification and that installation be done not negligently and recklessly.

speaker: Mr Christopher de Souza (Holland-Bukit Timah)
text: Would the Minister elaborate on how and whether the processes required will be raised so as to prevent another unfortunate event, such as that in Grenfell Tower in the United Kingdom (UK) or CIT Building on Toh Guan Road?

speaker: Mr Christopher de Souza (Holland-Bukit Timah)
text: Would the Minister elaborate how the stringency of the tests will balance between time and cost efficiency while minimising the chances of a costly misstep?

speaker: Mr Christopher de Souza (Holland-Bukit Timah)
text: The new section 22M requires alarm monitoring services to take all reasonable steps to check if there is a fire before cancelling.

speaker: Mr Christopher de Souza (Holland-Bukit Timah)
text: This offence reflects the great responsibility and heavy reliance the occupants of the building have on the alarm monitoring service.

speaker: Mr Christopher de Souza (Holland-Bukit Timah)
text: If the person carelessly cancels the call, the results may be devastating.

speaker: Mr Christopher de Souza (Holland-Bukit Timah)
text: By regulating alarm monitoring services and requiring a minimum standard of conduct, this Bill increases the teamwork among all stakeholders.

speaker: Mr Christopher de Souza (Holland-Bukit Timah)
text: On the issue of resource allocation, how is the Ministry raising awareness of the MyResponder app which allows members of the public to respond or send pictures of a fire?

speaker: Mr Christopher de Souza (Holland-Bukit Timah)
text: Additionally, how effective are public education efforts on how to manage chute fires, on where to find water sources to put out a fire and on how to react when a fire is at the entrance of the unit?

speaker: Mr Christopher de Souza (Holland-Bukit Timah)
text: Given the usefulness of the fire extinguisher in the event of a fire blocking the only escape pathway out of a house, what is being done to increase the take-up rate for fire extinguishers?

speaker: Mr Christopher de Souza (Holland-Bukit Timah)
text: That is equivalent to about 73% of the total number of cases last year and more than the total number of such cases in 2017.

speaker: Mr Christopher de Souza (Holland-Bukit Timah)
text: These fires, at least in residential premises, seem to have increased in severity.

speaker: Mr Christopher de Souza (Holland-Bukit Timah)
text: These numbers do not include the fires in July that were also caused by PABs or PMDs based on investigations or preliminary investigations: 3 July in Tampines; 9 July in Upper Boon Keng Road; 14 July in Yishun; 18 July in Bukit Batok which cost someone’s life; 22 July in Ang Mo Kio where three units were destroyed; 27 July, again in Boon Lay Drive.

speaker: Mr Christopher de Souza (Holland-Bukit Timah)
text: About six fires were reported in the media as of 28 July.

speaker: Mr Christopher de Souza (Holland-Bukit Timah)
text: The numbers seemed to have increased at a significant rate but, unlike chute fires which are the highest cause of fire, fires caused by PMDs are not easily fought by a layman.

speaker: Mr Christopher de Souza (Holland-Bukit Timah)
text: Some of these do not meet the UL-2272 certification requirement.

speaker: Mr Christopher de Souza (Holland-Bukit Timah)
text: They are like possibly ticking time bombs, unpredictable as to when and where the next fire will happen.

speaker: Mr Christopher de Souza (Holland-Bukit Timah)
text: Would the Ministry consider working closely with the Ministry of Transport (MOT) to hasten the timeframe by which all PMDs must meet the fire safety requirement?

speaker: Mr Christopher de Souza (Holland-Bukit Timah)
text: At this juncture, I want to take this opportunity to put on record the stellar work of the SCDF officers.

speaker: Mr Christopher de Souza (Holland-Bukit Timah)
text: In Jalan Buroh, on 21 June, the SCDF battled for about six hours a fire the size of two football fields, involving an unprecedented number of highly flammable liquified petroleum gas cylinders, fighting hard to contain and to put it out.

speaker: Mr Christopher de Souza (Holland-Bukit Timah)
text: In Woodlands, on 9 April, SCDF officers forced entry into a unit, rescued a woman, a teenager and two children trapped in the kitchen area, evacuated residents of other flats and put out the raging fire.

speaker: Mr Christopher de Souza (Holland-Bukit Timah)
text: In the process, one of the SCDF firefighters was injured with burns.

speaker: Mr Christopher de Souza (Holland-Bukit Timah)
text: In the fire in Ang Mo Kio on 22 July, the SCDF rescued from the burning flat a mother and her young children who were huddled in a room, too afraid to get out after hearing the explosion of the PMD.

speaker: Mr Christopher de Souza (Holland-Bukit Timah)
text: In the early hours of 18 July in Bukit Batok, SCDF officers in the call of duty wore breathing apparatus, cut through the iron gate, prised open the wooden door, rescuing a man who lay unconscious on the floor and his wife from the burning flat.

speaker: Mr Christopher de Souza (Holland-Bukit Timah)
text: These are just some examples of the life-saving courageous work that our SCDF officers do.

speaker: Mr Christopher de Souza (Holland-Bukit Timah)
text: It is not easy, especially when situations do not pan out the way everyone hopes for.

speaker: Mr Christopher de Souza (Holland-Bukit Timah)
text: Yet, these officers continue to be vigilant day in and day out, night in and night out, ready to put out the next fire, risking limb and possibly life, and saving lives.

speaker: Mr Christopher de Souza (Holland-Bukit Timah)
text: And having worked in the Government Parliamentary Committee (GPC), we understand first-hand the good work that the SCDF officers do.

speaker: Mr Christopher de Souza (Holland-Bukit Timah)
text: It involves the people who design the building, the builders and those who install fire safety devices, those who distribute and manufacture the fire safety devices, those who provide alarm monitoring services, tenants who place items in the passageway or engage in activities that potentially create an unreasonable fire hazard.

speaker: Mr Christopher de Souza (Holland-Bukit Timah)
text: In all, because no man is an island, I hope that we live together responsibly in our island city, working hand in hand to minimise fire hazards.

speaker: Er Dr Lee Bee Wah (Nee Soon)
text: There are cases when fires occurred in Housing and Development Board (HDB) and commercial units and did not spread.

speaker: Er Dr Lee Bee Wah (Nee Soon)
text: That is due to the equipment of necessary fire safety features, strict regulations in our fire safety code on usage of construction material that restricts flammability and permeation of flames and, of course, the efficiency of SCDF in reacting to fire emergencies.

speaker: Er Dr Lee Bee Wah (Nee Soon)
text: I wish to take this opportunity to express my appreciation to SCDF for their good work in keeping Singapore safe.

speaker: Er Dr Lee Bee Wah (Nee Soon)
text: Older buildings without the necessary fire safety features remain at risk.

speaker: Er Dr Lee Bee Wah (Nee Soon)
text: The UK Grenfell fire disaster, while far from home, remains a stark reminder to developed countries of what could happen if building developers use inappropriate construction material and scrimp on fire safety features.

speaker: Er Dr Lee Bee Wah (Nee Soon)
text: An entire building was demolished, scores of people died, survivors left homeless and in despair.

speaker: Er Dr Lee Bee Wah (Nee Soon)
text: The incident prompted questions and concerns from myself and my colleagues about whether this could happen in Singapore.

speaker: Er Dr Lee Bee Wah (Nee Soon)
text: Over the years, we talked about the need for greater vigilance against fires and, personally, I had advocated for the installation of safety features like smoke detectors in all public rental flats, a project which kickstarted last year and is currently underway.

speaker: Er Dr Lee Bee Wah (Nee Soon)
text: Today, I am glad to see the results of a comprehensive review that will bring about many enhancements to current fire safety policies.

speaker: Er Dr Lee Bee Wah (Nee Soon)
text: Everyone in the supply chain has a role to play and must be held responsible, not just the engineers, architects or the Registered Inspectors.

speaker: Er Dr Lee Bee Wah (Nee Soon)
text: Contractors, subcontractors, material suppliers, testing labs – all need to carry out their work professionally and honestly.

speaker: Er Dr Lee Bee Wah (Nee Soon)
text: Those who fall short shall be taken to task by this Fire Safety Act.

speaker: Er Dr Lee Bee Wah (Nee Soon)
text: As our buildings get older, extreme weather conditions and lack of maintenance could affect and even speed up the ageing process.

speaker: Er Dr Lee Bee Wah (Nee Soon)
text: It is imperative that safety checks are done regularly on these buildings.

speaker: Er Dr Lee Bee Wah (Nee Soon)
text: I am glad to note that SCDF will soon be able to appoint authorised third parties to conduct routine fire safety enforcement checks and building inspections.

speaker: Er Dr Lee Bee Wah (Nee Soon)
text: Understandably, SCDF may not have the resources on top of their regular duties, and plan to outsource this operation.

speaker: Er Dr Lee Bee Wah (Nee Soon)
text: I note that these authorised third parties would comprise Auxiliary Police Officers, retired SCDF and Police Officers as well as other public servants.

speaker: Er Dr Lee Bee Wah (Nee Soon)
text: What criteria and benchmarks would SCDF use to determine whether selected candidates are suitable for the roles?

speaker: Er Dr Lee Bee Wah (Nee Soon)
text: Would SCDF also consider registered fire safety engineers from the private sector and, if so, would they be required to submit a tender for their proposed services?

speaker: Er Dr Lee Bee Wah (Nee Soon)
text: In some industries, the competition in fees is so fierce that the fees become ridiculously low.

speaker: Er Dr Lee Bee Wah (Nee Soon)
text: As a result, the quality of the checks suffers.

speaker: Er Dr Lee Bee Wah (Nee Soon)
text: I hope SCDF will not let this happen to the fire safety checking profession.

speaker: Er Dr Lee Bee Wah (Nee Soon)
text: How often will these third-party operations be audited by SCDF?

speaker: Er Dr Lee Bee Wah (Nee Soon)
text: With the requirement for body-worn cameras, will the footage be reviewed regularly?

speaker: Er Dr Lee Bee Wah (Nee Soon)
text: What are issues that SCDF foresees that would justify the need for body cameras?

speaker: Er Dr Lee Bee Wah (Nee Soon)
text: These inspections and reviews would cost time and resources.

speaker: Er Dr Lee Bee Wah (Nee Soon)
text: Will the Government shoulder the expenses or is it the building owner who has to pay for these inspections and rectifications?

speaker: Er Dr Lee Bee Wah (Nee Soon)
text: What is the timeframe given for the building owners to comply?

speaker: Er Dr Lee Bee Wah (Nee Soon)
text: And what if they fail to do so?

speaker: Er Dr Lee Bee Wah (Nee Soon)
text: What if they dispute the order and drag out the case?

speaker: Er Dr Lee Bee Wah (Nee Soon)
text: Would this then result in the occupants and visitors being exposed to a fire safety issue whenever they are in the building?

speaker: Er Dr Lee Bee Wah (Nee Soon)
text: On the other hand, there may be some practical reasons causing failure to comply.

speaker: Er Dr Lee Bee Wah (Nee Soon)
text: Perhaps, the building owner may not have other plans for the property, or he or she could be away and the stand-in is unable to make the financial decisions.

speaker: Er Dr Lee Bee Wah (Nee Soon)
text: What will be done to speed up the process?

speaker: Er Dr Lee Bee Wah (Nee Soon)
text: Can the Minister share the projected timeline for the completion of fire safety upgrades in all these 500 or so buildings?

speaker: Er Dr Lee Bee Wah (Nee Soon)
text: Every single person has an important role to play in fire safety.

speaker: Er Dr Lee Bee Wah (Nee Soon)
text: Should they act irresponsibly and recklessly, thus putting the lives of other people in danger, they deserve a heavier punishment as a form of deterrence.

speaker: Er Dr Lee Bee Wah (Nee Soon)
text: I note that harsher penalties will apply to certain offences that compromise fire safety.

speaker: Er Dr Lee Bee Wah (Nee Soon)
text: But what about the people who practise dangerous PMD-charging habits and put themselves and their fellow occupants and neighbours in danger?

speaker: Er Dr Lee Bee Wah (Nee Soon)
text: We need to hold people accountable for practising unsafe charging practices, selling or buying not original and non-complying PMDs, batteries or chargers.

speaker: Er Dr Lee Bee Wah (Nee Soon)
text: This has been in the news lately and many of my residents are very concerned.

speaker: Er Dr Lee Bee Wah (Nee Soon)
text: We need to have more education, such as the proper way of charging, use of original parts, non-leaking batteries, non-faulty chargers, and no illegal modifications and so on.

speaker: Er Dr Lee Bee Wah (Nee Soon)
text: For those who buy or sell non-compliant PMDs or modify their PMDs, they deserve harsher punishment.

speaker: Er Dr Lee Bee Wah (Nee Soon)
text: There are also a lot of people who shop online.

speaker: Er Dr Lee Bee Wah (Nee Soon)
text: How is the Ministry going to regulate this?

speaker: Er Dr Lee Bee Wah (Nee Soon)
text: Many residents also ask: is there any place that buyers can send their PMDs for checking for compliance, just like Vicom checks for cars?

speaker: Er Dr Lee Bee Wah (Nee Soon)
text: Residents want to be law-abiding, but they do not know how to go about it.

speaker: Er Dr Lee Bee Wah (Nee Soon)
text: For MOE, I hope it can include compulsory modules in school on safe riding, correct etiquette and the right way of charging and so on.

speaker: Er Dr Lee Bee Wah (Nee Soon)
text: If we cannot tackle the current PMD problem satisfactorily, I would like to give a bold suggestion – ban PMDs totally, personal mobility aids (PMAs) excluded.

speaker: Er Dr Lee Bee Wah (Nee Soon)
text: Then step by step, issue licences to those who need them only after they have attended the compulsory courses, passed the exam, bought the third-party insurance.

speaker: Er Dr Lee Bee Wah (Nee Soon)
text: Just by registering PMDs alone is not good enough.

speaker: Er Dr Lee Bee Wah (Nee Soon)
text: We need the riders to be licensed, and the licences can be revoked if they cause serious injuries or death.

speaker: Er Dr Lee Bee Wah (Nee Soon)
text: These are the bold and decisive actions that I hope our multi-agencies can seriously look into.

speaker: Er Dr Lee Bee Wah (Nee Soon)
text: (In Mandarin):   I appreciate that the authorities are paying close attention to the fire safety issue.

speaker: Er Dr Lee Bee Wah (Nee Soon)
text: I lived in the countryside when I was a kid.

speaker: Er Dr Lee Bee Wah (Nee Soon)
text: I remember that when villagers gathered together to chit-chat, their face would turn whenever the topic of "tiger" came up.

speaker: Er Dr Lee Bee Wah (Nee Soon)
text: Similarly, today at coffee shops, when residents gather together to talk, their face would turn when the topic of "PMD" comes up.

speaker: Er Dr Lee Bee Wah (Nee Soon)
text: One resident said: “In the daytime, when I walk on the pedestrian path, I always feel very intimidated.

speaker: Er Dr Lee Bee Wah (Nee Soon)
text: I will have to keep looking to the right and left so that I won’t be knocked down by PMDs.

speaker: Er Dr Lee Bee Wah (Nee Soon)
text: At night, I even have nightmares because I do not know when my neighbour’s PMD will catch fire”.

speaker: Er Dr Lee Bee Wah (Nee Soon)
text: This is the suffering that our residents have to endure ever since the PMDs are introduced into Singapore.

speaker: Er Dr Lee Bee Wah (Nee Soon)
text: I hope that all the Government agencies can work together to solve this problem.

speaker: Er Dr Lee Bee Wah (Nee Soon)
text: We should also help PMD users to check if their PMDs are compliant to the standard and teach them the correct ways to charge their PMDs.

speaker: Er Dr Lee Bee Wah (Nee Soon)
text: If we cannot tackle the current safety problems brought about by riding a PMD or charging it, I would suggest we ban the PMDs temporarily.

speaker: Er Dr Lee Bee Wah (Nee Soon)
text: In the future, we should only issue licences to those who have attended the mandatory courses and passed the exams, bought third-party insurance, and whose PMDs are compliant to the fire safety standard.

speaker: Er Dr Lee Bee Wah (Nee Soon)
text: Otherwise, how can we ensure the safety of pedestrians and HDB residents?

speaker: Er Dr Lee Bee Wah (Nee Soon)
text: I hope that the relevant authorities can look into this matter seriously.

speaker: Ms Sylvia Lim (Aljunied)
text: There is a common occurrence of HDB bin chute fires, and electrical fires caused by overloading and charging e-scooters and batteries.

speaker: Ms Sylvia Lim (Aljunied)
text: The density of our high-rise environment makes fire safety critical.

speaker: Ms Sylvia Lim (Aljunied)
text: As such, I am supportive of the rationale of this Bill to give further authority to SCDF to require fire safety enhancements to buildings, to regulate fire safety products and to enhance SCDF investigation powers.

speaker: Ms Sylvia Lim (Aljunied)
text: Nevertheless, I wish to make some observations and seek clarification on three issues: first, imposing fire safety upgrades on existing buildings; second, the handling of the recent cases concerning non-compliant claddings; and third, the proposed use of third-party officers as routine inspectors.

speaker: Ms Sylvia Lim (Aljunied)
text: This will effectively mean that buildings that were compliant with fire safety requirements at the time they were constructed, may have additional requirements imposed on them.

speaker: Ms Sylvia Lim (Aljunied)
text: In the Ministry of Home Affairs (MHA) press release of 8 July, it was stated that in imposing these additional requirements on existing buildings, SCDF would adopt a judicious, risk-based approach in identifying buildings for fire safety upgrades.

speaker: Ms Sylvia Lim (Aljunied)
text: It was further stated that in deciding whether to impose such requirements, SCDF would consider the buildings’ fire risk profile and factors, such as building age, purpose and the profile of its occupants.

speaker: Ms Sylvia Lim (Aljunied)
text: I also understand the sentiments of Er Dr Lee Bee Wah on this matter, just expressed.

speaker: Ms Sylvia Lim (Aljunied)
text: At the same time, I note that SCDF has mentioned that it would be judicious in its approach.

speaker: Ms Sylvia Lim (Aljunied)
text: There is, indeed, a need to assess each older building to determine whether the upgrades are critical for safety, or are good-to-haves which may be costly and have limited utility.

speaker: Ms Sylvia Lim (Aljunied)
text: About six years ago, a cluster of seven Housing and Urban Development Company (HUDC) blocks in my ward at Serangoon North built in the 1980s underwent privatisation.

speaker: Ms Sylvia Lim (Aljunied)
text: In connection with this exercise, the residents were advised that they needed to do A&A works to bring the cluster up to the current requirements of the Fire Code.

speaker: Ms Sylvia Lim (Aljunied)
text: The residents then undertook the works, such as installing fire doors at every staircase landing and making enhancements to their lifts.

speaker: Ms Sylvia Lim (Aljunied)
text: These works caused ground frustration as they affected residents’ daily lives in terms of inconvenience, dust and lift shutdowns, and also involved expenditure.

speaker: Ms Sylvia Lim (Aljunied)
text: After the estate was privatised in 2014, discussions resumed to obtain approval for an en bloc sale of the estate.

speaker: Ms Sylvia Lim (Aljunied)
text: Within three years, the estate was sold en bloc to a developer.

speaker: Ms Sylvia Lim (Aljunied)
text: If you were to visit the site today, you will see that all the former blocks have been demolished.

speaker: Ms Sylvia Lim (Aljunied)
text: That leads to a reasonable question: to what end then were the fire safety enhancements made to the old blocks?

speaker: Ms Sylvia Lim (Aljunied)
text: Moving forward, while the HUDC privatisation is over, there may be older buildings that are expected to be sold to developers or be otherwise redeveloped.

speaker: Ms Sylvia Lim (Aljunied)
text: Can MHA elaborate on the judicious risk-based approach that SCDF will undertake in deciding whether certain upgrades are critical?

speaker: Ms Sylvia Lim (Aljunied)
text: The fatal fires at Toh Guan Road and London’s Grenfell Tower were a wake-up call.

speaker: Ms Sylvia Lim (Aljunied)
text: After the Grenfell Tower tragedy, I filed a Parliamentary Question asking what preliminary lessons could be learnt.

speaker: Ms Sylvia Lim (Aljunied)
text: The Minister’s reply then was that SCDF would study the investigation report of the London Fire Brigade when it was released, to see if changes to our fire regulations were needed.

speaker: Ms Sylvia Lim (Aljunied)
text: In addition, he touched on the existing regulatory regime for construction projects, where the registered Qualified Person (QP) was responsible for ensuring that building materials conformed to the prevailing Fire Code.

speaker: Ms Sylvia Lim (Aljunied)
text: Among the requirements were that all claddings used in buildings had to meet the stringent Class Zero industry standard.

speaker: Ms Sylvia Lim (Aljunied)
text: It was further stated that after the QP signed off, a Registered Inspector would have to inspect the building to ensure that all fire safety requirements had been met.

speaker: Ms Sylvia Lim (Aljunied)
text: I assume that many of these buildings would have been issued with Fire Safety Certificates by SCDF, indicating that they were compliant with requirements.

speaker: Ms Sylvia Lim (Aljunied)
text: Be that as it may, SCDF has since reviewed the regulatory regime and identified points of weakness that led to non-compliant materials being used.

speaker: Ms Sylvia Lim (Aljunied)
text: These gaps involved the upstream supply chain, from manufacture and storage to testing and supply.

speaker: Ms Sylvia Lim (Aljunied)
text: There were instances of materials of different gradings being mixed and stored in the same place without proper distinguishing marks.

speaker: Ms Sylvia Lim (Aljunied)
text: To address this, the Bill introduces the new Part V on regulated fire safety products to tighten those weaknesses in the supply chain.

speaker: Ms Sylvia Lim (Aljunied)
text: Are SCDF investigations still ongoing into other cases of non-compliant cladding being supplied and used, and whether other offences were disclosed?

speaker: Ms Sylvia Lim (Aljunied)
text: Could the Ministry explain what role SCDF played in assisting or supporting these innocent parties during the rectification works?

speaker: Ms Sylvia Lim (Aljunied)
text: I have a query about third-party officers to be appointed.

speaker: Ms Sylvia Lim (Aljunied)
text: MHA has stated that the rationale for this supplementary resource is to allow SCDF officers to focus on more complex enforcement inspections.

speaker: Ms Sylvia Lim (Aljunied)
text: These third-party officers would be deemed public servants under the Penal Code and receive the protections under the Penal Code.

speaker: Ms Sylvia Lim (Aljunied)
text: According to the proposed section 8F, such persons are to be individually appointed and could include employees of a public authority.

speaker: Ms Sylvia Lim (Aljunied)
text: Would these third-party officers be restricted to Singaporeans and Permanent Residents, or would foreigners also be eligible for these deployments?

speaker: Ms Sylvia Lim (Aljunied)
text: Earlier, the Senior Parliamentary Secretary explained how these outsourced inspectors would take over visits to premises.

speaker: Ms Sylvia Lim (Aljunied)
text: Is there any concern that SCDF may lose valuable ground knowledge by outsourcing routine inspections?

speaker: Ms Sylvia Lim (Aljunied)
text: I am supportive of the Bill and would also like to take this opportunity to thank SCDF for its important and life-saving work.

speaker: Ms Sylvia Lim (Aljunied)
text: Nevertheless, for a better understanding of how the regime would work, it would be most helpful if my queries could be addressed.

speaker: Assoc Prof Walter Theseira (Nominated Member)
text: Singapore’s fire casualty rates consistently rank among the safest worldwide.

speaker: Assoc Prof Walter Theseira (Nominated Member)
text: The impact of our fires on human life was also less severe, with only 0.04 fire deaths per 100,000 people.

speaker: Assoc Prof Walter Theseira (Nominated Member)
text: So, we are building on a strong base of fire safety with this Bill.

speaker: Assoc Prof Walter Theseira (Nominated Member)
text: As of 2018, we have nearly one million owner-occupied HDB flats in Singapore.

speaker: Assoc Prof Walter Theseira (Nominated Member)
text: Nearly all were built before HFADs became mandatory for new flats in June 2018.

speaker: Assoc Prof Walter Theseira (Nominated Member)
text: Like many Singaporeans, I live in an older HDB flat.

speaker: Assoc Prof Walter Theseira (Nominated Member)
text: HFADs were not common in Singapore when my flat was built.

speaker: Assoc Prof Walter Theseira (Nominated Member)
text: They were not even a consideration for my parents or the older generation when they moved in.

speaker: Assoc Prof Walter Theseira (Nominated Member)
text: Perhaps we can assume that the vast majority of HDB flats have no HFADs.

speaker: Assoc Prof Walter Theseira (Nominated Member)
text: We have seen published equipment costs of $50 to $80 for a HFAD with a 10-year battery.

speaker: Assoc Prof Walter Theseira (Nominated Member)
text: In 2018, there was the SG Bonus which gave all Singaporeans a cash payout of up to $300.

speaker: Assoc Prof Walter Theseira (Nominated Member)
text: We are clearly prepared to spend even larger sums than $160 million on the welfare of Singaporeans.

speaker: Assoc Prof Walter Theseira (Nominated Member)
text: As an economist, I normally find myself suggesting that the Government should spend money cautiously and should not interfere unnecessarily in private markets.

speaker: Assoc Prof Walter Theseira (Nominated Member)
text: But I think there are a few inherent market failures in the private provision of fire safety.

speaker: Assoc Prof Walter Theseira (Nominated Member)
text: Singaporeans lack information to make wise choices on home fire safety.

speaker: Assoc Prof Walter Theseira (Nominated Member)
text: There are benefits not just to homeowners, but also external benefits to the community.

speaker: Assoc Prof Walter Theseira (Nominated Member)
text: Taken together, I do not think we will invest the right amount in home fire safety if we just leave it to the private market.

speaker: Assoc Prof Walter Theseira (Nominated Member)
text: So, first, Singaporeans have little experience with HFADs and they do not know the costs and benefits of installing and maintaining these devices.

speaker: Assoc Prof Walter Theseira (Nominated Member)
text: In some developed countries, these devices have been mandatory for many years.

speaker: Assoc Prof Walter Theseira (Nominated Member)
text: Homeowners may have to adjust their cooking habits, such as ensuring that ventilation prevents cooking smoke from triggering the alarm.

speaker: Assoc Prof Walter Theseira (Nominated Member)
text: We cannot leave it up to the community to make a wise decision just on their own.

speaker: Assoc Prof Walter Theseira (Nominated Member)
text: Second, there are real benefits of installing HFADs to homeowners and to the community.

speaker: Assoc Prof Walter Theseira (Nominated Member)
text: Other research finds that HFADs are the least likely to be installed or working in homes which face higher risks, such as those occupied by elderly residents.

speaker: Assoc Prof Walter Theseira (Nominated Member)
text: Third, I am sorry to say, light-touch interventions may not help improve fire safety.

speaker: Assoc Prof Walter Theseira (Nominated Member)
text: In a paper titled "Interventions for promoting smoke alarm ownership and function", published in the Cochrane Database of Systematic Reviews in 2001, researchers found that programmes that educate the public on HFADs have only modest effects in increasing installation rates.

speaker: Assoc Prof Walter Theseira (Nominated Member)
text: Community programmes that gave away HFADs actually had no effect.

speaker: Assoc Prof Walter Theseira (Nominated Member)
text: For most of us, a home fire is a remote risk which simply is not salient, PMD fires aside.

speaker: Assoc Prof Walter Theseira (Nominated Member)
text: It is not a financial cost issue for many.

speaker: Assoc Prof Walter Theseira (Nominated Member)
text: It is actually a mental bandwidth cost issue.

speaker: Assoc Prof Walter Theseira (Nominated Member)
text: We have other things to do and installing a Home Fire Alarm is a low priority.

speaker: Assoc Prof Walter Theseira (Nominated Member)
text: If we aspire towards a high rate of Home Fire Alarm installation, I am forced to the conclusion that only a mandatory, Government-funded programme is likely to have significant effects.

speaker: Assoc Prof Walter Theseira (Nominated Member)
text: Fourth, we have an ageing population that inherently faces higher risks from home fires.

speaker: Assoc Prof Walter Theseira (Nominated Member)
text: Cooking fires are more likely to be forgotten by the elderly.

speaker: Assoc Prof Walter Theseira (Nominated Member)
text: Physical limitations make it more likely that accidents will happen with oil lamps and incense.

speaker: Assoc Prof Walter Theseira (Nominated Member)
text: Some psychological conditions often found in the elderly, such as hoarding disorders, may also contribute to fire risks.

speaker: Assoc Prof Walter Theseira (Nominated Member)
text: Our ageing population also tend to live in older flats, which have older wiring and electrical infrastructure.

speaker: Assoc Prof Walter Theseira (Nominated Member)
text: Assistance devices for the elderly, such as motorised wheelchairs, rely on lithium batteries which must be charged.

speaker: Assoc Prof Walter Theseira (Nominated Member)
text: And if a fire does break out, an older population is less able to react quickly to put out the fire or to escape.

speaker: Assoc Prof Walter Theseira (Nominated Member)
text: The extra seconds or minutes that a HFAD gives for warning could be critical.

speaker: Assoc Prof Walter Theseira (Nominated Member)
text: If we are agreed that installation of HFADs will benefit HDB residents and the community, then we should do this as efficiently as possible.

speaker: Assoc Prof Walter Theseira (Nominated Member)
text: I believe there will be considerable economies of scale from having installation carried out by contractors appointed through a rigorous tender process.

speaker: Assoc Prof Walter Theseira (Nominated Member)
text: The contractors will buy in bulk and develop standardised processes for installation.

speaker: Assoc Prof Walter Theseira (Nominated Member)
text: This will be much cheaper than having residents individually engage contractors.

speaker: Assoc Prof Walter Theseira (Nominated Member)
text: These opportunists take advantage of our citizens’ lack of information on fire safety.

speaker: Assoc Prof Walter Theseira (Nominated Member)
text: Many residents have encountered door-to-door salesmen selling fire protection equipment.

speaker: Assoc Prof Walter Theseira (Nominated Member)
text: A friend, who has a Doctorate in Philosophy (PhD), bought a fire extinguisher from such a salesperson, thinking that they were acting with the support of the authorities.

speaker: Assoc Prof Walter Theseira (Nominated Member)
text: Of course, it is good to have fire safety devices at home.

speaker: Assoc Prof Walter Theseira (Nominated Member)
text: But we should try to avoid enriching rent-seekers in the process.

speaker: Assoc Prof Walter Theseira (Nominated Member)
text: Indeed, without proper education, it is unlikely that installed HFADs will be maintained effectively.

speaker: Assoc Prof Walter Theseira (Nominated Member)
text: A resident who experiences false alarms because the device is installed too close to cooking smoke, for example, may just disable the device instead of relocating it.

speaker: Assoc Prof Walter Theseira (Nominated Member)
text: I do not think we can rely on these private opportunists to educate the public properly.

speaker: Assoc Prof Walter Theseira (Nominated Member)
text: I think this is also important, but the economies of scale are very different.

speaker: Assoc Prof Walter Theseira (Nominated Member)
text: There are a huge variety of floor plans and designs of private condominiums and homes.

speaker: Assoc Prof Walter Theseira (Nominated Member)
text: The economies of scale from a centralised, coordinated programme are likely to be much smaller, compared to HDB housing where a standardised process for installation can be developed.

speaker: Assoc Prof Daniel Goh Pei Siong (Non-Constituency Member)
text: This Bill will further strengthen our fire safety regime by enhancing SCDF’s regulatory and enforcement powers and optimising SCDF’s resources.

speaker: Assoc Prof Daniel Goh Pei Siong (Non-Constituency Member)
text: It is commendable that the Ministry believes that, while the number of fire incidents has been stable, the fire safety regulations must be updated regularly to keep pace with the times, especially with evolving fire safety risks.

speaker: Assoc Prof Daniel Goh Pei Siong (Non-Constituency Member)
text: It is crucial to pre-empt and plug possible developing gaps in the fire safety regime.

speaker: Assoc Prof Daniel Goh Pei Siong (Non-Constituency Member)
text: There is a developing gap that the Bill may not have adequately addressed.

speaker: Assoc Prof Daniel Goh Pei Siong (Non-Constituency Member)
text: This is a gap emerging from the convergence of three trends: one, an ageing society; two, ageing HDB buildings; and three, the adoption of new technologies.

speaker: Assoc Prof Daniel Goh Pei Siong (Non-Constituency Member)
text: Back in November 2017, I asked the Ministry of Trade and Industry in Parliament whether the batteries for PMDs are covered under the Consumer Protection (Safety Requirements) Regulations as controlled goods, because the number of fires caused by PMD batteries charging overnight was increasing.

speaker: Assoc Prof Daniel Goh Pei Siong (Non-Constituency Member)
text: Senior Minister of State Dr Koh Poh Koon acknowledged then that there was a slight increase in incidence of such electric fires and said this was something the Standards, Productivity and Innovation Board (SPRING) Singapore could look into.

speaker: Assoc Prof Daniel Goh Pei Siong (Non-Constituency Member)
text: Since then, the slight increase has become quite a worrying spike.

speaker: Assoc Prof Daniel Goh Pei Siong (Non-Constituency Member)
text: The Senior Minister of State for Transport has already addressed the issue of fires related to PMD batteries in the Ministerial Statement earlier.

speaker: Assoc Prof Daniel Goh Pei Siong (Non-Constituency Member)
text: It is good that the ban on the use of non-UL2272 PMDs on public paths has been brought forward.

speaker: Assoc Prof Daniel Goh Pei Siong (Non-Constituency Member)
text: Hopefully, this will greatly mitigate the problem of fires involving PMD batteries.

speaker: Assoc Prof Daniel Goh Pei Siong (Non-Constituency Member)
text: But even as we solve this problem of PMD fires, there will be unexpected fire safety challenges cropping up in the near future with regard to the adoption of new technology.

speaker: Assoc Prof Daniel Goh Pei Siong (Non-Constituency Member)
text: Our homes are becoming charging points for all kinds of devices and there will be more to come with fast improving drone and smart home technologies.

speaker: Assoc Prof Daniel Goh Pei Siong (Non-Constituency Member)
text: Furthermore, ageing HDB flats built for Industry 2.0 and 3.0 will face problems with electrical load and lack the most modern fire safety features.

speaker: Assoc Prof Daniel Goh Pei Siong (Non-Constituency Member)
text: An ageing population will also require a rethink of fire safety provisions and contingencies, as seniors are less alert and less mobile in fire situations.

speaker: Assoc Prof Daniel Goh Pei Siong (Non-Constituency Member)
text: I will highlight four issues here in the context of the fire safety provisions enhanced by this Bill.

speaker: Assoc Prof Daniel Goh Pei Siong (Non-Constituency Member)
text: The first issue is the retrofitting of HDB flats with smoke detectors.

speaker: Assoc Prof Daniel Goh Pei Siong (Non-Constituency Member)
text: This Bill empowers SCDF to mandate building owners to install critical fire safety upgrades, particularly fire alarm systems.

speaker: Assoc Prof Daniel Goh Pei Siong (Non-Constituency Member)
text: It is said that SCDF will adopt a judicious, risk-based approach and this provision is largely targeted at ageing commercial and industrial buildings.

speaker: Assoc Prof Daniel Goh Pei Siong (Non-Constituency Member)
text: If this is so important, would SCDF work with HDB to retrofit all public housing flats with HFADs?

speaker: Assoc Prof Daniel Goh Pei Siong (Non-Constituency Member)
text: If it has to be done in phases, as I imagine such a major exercise requires, flats that have undergone or are undergoing the Home Improvement Programme renovations should be retrofitted first.

speaker: Assoc Prof Daniel Goh Pei Siong (Non-Constituency Member)
text: This will benefit the vast majority of the population and protect most Singaporeans.

speaker: Assoc Prof Daniel Goh Pei Siong (Non-Constituency Member)
text: After all, the PMD fire experience has shown us that neighbours are the ones who need to be alerted early to such quick and ferocious fires, even if the fires are contained by units designed as fire compartments.

speaker: Assoc Prof Daniel Goh Pei Siong (Non-Constituency Member)
text: Perhaps a smoke detector would have done the job of alerting the four people early to give them time to evacuate.

speaker: Assoc Prof Daniel Goh Pei Siong (Non-Constituency Member)
text: The second issue is the consideration of upgrades to cater to seniors living in HDB blocks.

speaker: Assoc Prof Daniel Goh Pei Siong (Non-Constituency Member)
text: The Fire Code has been revised to require super high-rise residential buildings, which go beyond 40 storeys, to have refuge floors with holding areas at 20-storey intervals and two fire lifts to facilitate evacuation of persons with disabilities and seniors by firefighters.

speaker: Assoc Prof Daniel Goh Pei Siong (Non-Constituency Member)
text: However, even this may not be enough in view of ageing HDB flats and the ageing population.

speaker: Assoc Prof Daniel Goh Pei Siong (Non-Constituency Member)
text: In a fire on the 48th floor at Pinnacle Duxton in May 2018, many residents, especially seniors, chose to use lifts to evacuate despite knowing the risk.

speaker: Assoc Prof Daniel Goh Pei Siong (Non-Constituency Member)
text: A senior citizen aged 64 walked down three floors before giving up and taking the lift.

speaker: Assoc Prof Daniel Goh Pei Siong (Non-Constituency Member)
text: Many ageing HDB blocks are 10 to 24 storeys high.

speaker: Assoc Prof Daniel Goh Pei Siong (Non-Constituency Member)
text: A senior citizen like the one at Pinnacle Duxton who gave up after walking down three floors would face the same problem of evacuating an older, relatively low-rise HDB block.

speaker: Assoc Prof Daniel Goh Pei Siong (Non-Constituency Member)
text: Would the retrofitting of such blocks with refuge floors with holding areas, say, at one of the staircase landings or fire lift lobbies of common corridors every four to five storeys, better cater to an ageing society?

speaker: Assoc Prof Daniel Goh Pei Siong (Non-Constituency Member)
text: We should also be more concerned with HDB studio apartment and 2-room blocks built for senior citizens.

speaker: Assoc Prof Daniel Goh Pei Siong (Non-Constituency Member)
text: These blocks have smaller units that are packed more closely together, which means a fire could potentially spread more quickly, compared to other HDB blocks.

speaker: Assoc Prof Daniel Goh Pei Siong (Non-Constituency Member)
text: This is aggravated by the concentration of senior citizens in such blocks.

speaker: Assoc Prof Daniel Goh Pei Siong (Non-Constituency Member)
text: I have made the point about retrofitting all HDB flats with smoke detectors.

speaker: Assoc Prof Daniel Goh Pei Siong (Non-Constituency Member)
text: I believe studio apartment and 2-room HDB blocks should be prioritised for such retrofitting, as our senior citizens require protection most urgently.

speaker: Assoc Prof Daniel Goh Pei Siong (Non-Constituency Member)
text: This is a good move, not only because it frees up SCDF officers for complex enforcement checks, but also because it allows SCDF to scale up routine fire safety checks.

speaker: Assoc Prof Daniel Goh Pei Siong (Non-Constituency Member)
text: This means two things can be done for ageing HDB flats.

speaker: Assoc Prof Daniel Goh Pei Siong (Non-Constituency Member)
text: First, the frequency of routine fire safety checks can be increased for ageing HDB flats.

speaker: Assoc Prof Daniel Goh Pei Siong (Non-Constituency Member)
text: Second, SCDF officers can focus on mapping the specific fire risks of ageing HDB blocks in light of the ageing population, so that fire safety features can be customised for each block.

speaker: Assoc Prof Daniel Goh Pei Siong (Non-Constituency Member)
text: As the Ministry would know, HDB block designs are very diverse because of our public housing place-making efforts and efforts to cater to different demographic and income groups.

speaker: Assoc Prof Daniel Goh Pei Siong (Non-Constituency Member)
text: But this also means that fire safety risks differ from block to block.

speaker: Assoc Prof Daniel Goh Pei Siong (Non-Constituency Member)
text: Also, the actions of residents, by placing items in common corridors or modifying their flats during renovations, affect the fire safety risks differently.

speaker: Assoc Prof Daniel Goh Pei Siong (Non-Constituency Member)
text: An ageing population also means that more items will be placed in common areas and more renovations will be done.

speaker: Assoc Prof Daniel Goh Pei Siong (Non-Constituency Member)
text: General rules will apply, but there will be varied situations that require on-the-ground interpretation.

speaker: Assoc Prof Daniel Goh Pei Siong (Non-Constituency Member)
text: This will require SCDF to conduct more complex inspections.

speaker: Assoc Prof Daniel Goh Pei Siong (Non-Constituency Member)
text: Other than mapping the fire risks of ageing HDB blocks, there is also the need to map the specific risks of HDB blocks with an ageing residential profile.

speaker: Assoc Prof Daniel Goh Pei Siong (Non-Constituency Member)
text: With new big data and data visualisation technologies, it should not be too difficult for HDB to provide regularly updated information to SCDF on HDB blocks that house more senior citizens across the city.

speaker: Assoc Prof Daniel Goh Pei Siong (Non-Constituency Member)
text: Armed with such knowledge, SCDF and the Police could deploy additional resources to assist in evacuation and support of senior citizens in the event of fire in blocks with higher concentrations of elderly residents.

speaker: Assoc Prof Daniel Goh Pei Siong (Non-Constituency Member)
text: If this is going to be a protocol for SCDF and the Police, it would be important to communicate this to Singaporeans for peace of mind.

speaker: Assoc Prof Daniel Goh Pei Siong (Non-Constituency Member)
text: The question is, will SCDF officers be empowered to enter into HDB flats to investigate fire safety violations and what are the likely violations in such scenarios?

speaker: Assoc Prof Daniel Goh Pei Siong (Non-Constituency Member)
text: I am asking this because I have seen a few cases of hoarding while assisting with constituency work in Aljunied Group Representation Constituency, where HDB flats are piled up high with flammables, such as newspapers and cardboard boxes.

speaker: Assoc Prof Daniel Goh Pei Siong (Non-Constituency Member)
text: The residents responsible for collecting and hoarding such materials are usually suffering from mental illnesses.

speaker: Assoc Prof Daniel Goh Pei Siong (Non-Constituency Member)
text: Neighbours are understandably very concerned about fire safety.

speaker: Assoc Prof Daniel Goh Pei Siong (Non-Constituency Member)
text: Due to the stigmatisation of mental illnesses, it has been difficult for many of the suffering residents to seek help themselves.

speaker: Assoc Prof Daniel Goh Pei Siong (Non-Constituency Member)
text: Their family members are also at a loss.

speaker: Assoc Prof Daniel Goh Pei Siong (Non-Constituency Member)
text: In one case I witnessed, multiple agencies were involved to try to resolve the matter – social workers from the Family Service Centre, healthcare workers from the Institute of Mental Health, HDB officers, Police Officers, SCDF officers, Town Council officers, Resident Committee members.

speaker: Assoc Prof Daniel Goh Pei Siong (Non-Constituency Member)
text: However, there was very little they could do unless the suffering resident volunteered to be helped.

speaker: Assoc Prof Daniel Goh Pei Siong (Non-Constituency Member)
text: I would expect the number of such cases to increase as the society ages, especially with the increase in incidences of dementia.

speaker: Assoc Prof Daniel Goh Pei Siong (Non-Constituency Member)
text: On the one hand, forceful entry into the premises to investigate and intervene into fire risks may aggravate the resident's condition.

speaker: Assoc Prof Daniel Goh Pei Siong (Non-Constituency Member)
text: On the other hand, the resident and the neighbours cannot be expected to live with the fire risks indefinitely.

speaker: Assoc Prof Daniel Goh Pei Siong (Non-Constituency Member)
text: Deputy Speaker, Sir, our society is ageing, our HDB flats are ageing, yet we are adopting new technologies that increase fire risks.

speaker: Assoc Prof Daniel Goh Pei Siong (Non-Constituency Member)
text: This Bill is a timely response, but even as we strengthen SCDF's powers, we need to review and update our fire safety regime for the trends taking shape in the near horizon.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: I have seen first-hand the amazing work our SCDF does and let me start by thanking them for keeping all of us safe and for risking their lives to save ours.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: I support the strengthening of SCDF's regulatory and enforcement powers and the increase in penalties for fire-related offences.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: I strongly support this as the fire alarm system provides early warning to occupants and can potentially save lives.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
