text: My question is, if we agree that having a fire alarm system saves lives, why do we not have it for our HDB flats?

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: It seems even stranger that we have fire alarm systems in our HDB multi-storey car parks where nobody lives and not in our HDB flats where hundreds of people live in?

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: I know the reply will be that "under our Fire Code, all residential units are designed as fire compartments, typically using fire-resistant walls and floors and fire-rated main entrance doors, to mitigate fire spread." But we know that this is not the case in recent fire incidences.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: Last year, I asked whether MHA will review the Fire Code and consider including in the Fire Code the installation of central fire alarm systems in HDB flats.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: This is a commendable move as the alarm will provide early warning to the occupants of the affected unit, so that they can take immediate steps to evacuate or extinguish the fire.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: Moving forward, does the Ministry have plans to further require all other HDB units to install HFADs?

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: We still have to remember that an HFAD will only alert the residents of an individual unit.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: Again, without a centralised fire alarm system, the only way of alerting other residents in the block of the fire is for our firemen, policemen or perhaps grassroots to go unit by unit, knocking on each and every door.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: This is incredibly inefficient, which possibly prolongs the exposure of residents to smoke which is well-known to be the most common cause of injury in fires.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: According to a study, it is the "inhalation of noxious gases rather than thermal injury" that leads to a fatality.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: I sincerely hope that MHA will consider mandating centralised fire alarm systems in every HDB block.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: Next, to make our HDB flats even safer, I hope that MHA mandates that every unit be fitted with a fire-rated door, even those facing an external corridor.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: I understand that the current thinking is that for flats, for units that face an external corridor, the smoke will dissipate outwards and away from the other units and, hence, SCDF's assessment is that there is no need for a fire-rated door to be installed for such units.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: But this was not the case for the fire that broke out in an Ang Mo Kio flat on 22 July that was raised earlier as well.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: SCDF said it rescued four people, including three children, from the neighbouring unit while the Police and SCDF personnel evacuated about 60 people from the affected blocks.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: This was an HDB unit facing an external corridor and the neighbouring units were affected.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: We recognise the effectiveness of fire-rated doors in slowing down the spread of fires and smoke.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: Why then do we not make this a requirement for all units?

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: I understand that they will have cost implications.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: However, given that residential fires are a real risk, the dividends of our investment in fire-rated doors will come in the form of lives saved and injuries prevented, which are priceless.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: For the centralised fire alarm systems, I also appreciate that there might be concerns about false alarms and people tampering with the alarm systems.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: But again, in this case, the pros heavily outweigh the cons.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: Fire alarms in all units, a centralised fire alarm system and fire-rated doors, will all help to save lives.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: Lastly, with regard to the appointment of third-party officers.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: The new section 8(F) provides for the appointment of "supplementary enforcement officers", or third parties to take charge of "routine fire safety enforcement checks and building inspections".

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: The rationale behind this amendment is for SCDF to focus its resources on "more complex" enforcement matters instead.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: First, these third-party officers have very broad and diverse powers and tasks.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: Can the Ministry clarify how these officers will be selected and "suitably trained" to ensure they can understand and perform their responsibilities just as effectively as an SCDF officer?

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: Second, I understand that these third-party officers will be subject to audits conducted by SCDF.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: Can the Senior Parliamentary Secretary share more about the scope and frequency of these audits?

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: Will the Senior Parliamentary Secretary or the Minister have oversight of the audit findings?

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: Third, can the Ministry consider implementing a reporting mechanism to ensure that third-party enforcement is being carried out in a fair and effective manner?

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: What other safeguards would be put in place to keep these officers in check?

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: Such checks and safeguards will be useful in ensuring that third-party officers are compliant with the provisions of this Act and carry out enforcement properly.

speaker: Dr Chia Shi-Lu (Tanjong Pagar)
text: Deputy Speaker, Sir, fire is a horrific event and the amendments to this Act are timely and will strike a balance between empowering SCDF, which has always been working tirelessly to keep us all safe from the scourge of fire, to continue upholding high fire safety standards and ensuring public safety as well as managing the costs for building owners and industry stakeholders.

speaker: Dr Chia Shi-Lu (Tanjong Pagar)
text: In Singapore, most fires are the results of accidents and, in some cases, negligence.

speaker: Dr Chia Shi-Lu (Tanjong Pagar)
text: But we should also be on guard against sabotage and attacks, including those related to criminal and terrorist activities.

speaker: Dr Chia Shi-Lu (Tanjong Pagar)
text: We can draw lessons from fire incidents in other countries.

speaker: Dr Chia Shi-Lu (Tanjong Pagar)
text: First, allow me to comment on the need for critical fire safety features for all buildings.

speaker: Dr Chia Shi-Lu (Tanjong Pagar)
text: Hence, I fully support the proposal to require owners of older buildings to upgrade and install critical fire safety features to keep up with the latest Fire Code.

speaker: Dr Chia Shi-Lu (Tanjong Pagar)
text: In particular, I hope to see wider adoption of smoke detection and sprinkler systems in all buildings by owners.

speaker: Dr Chia Shi-Lu (Tanjong Pagar)
text: Such features are necessary, regardless of the size or the designated building use.

speaker: Dr Chia Shi-Lu (Tanjong Pagar)
text: As the Kyoto Animation fire had shown, regulators should not make exemptions, as precious lives are at stake and fires consume buildings both big and small.

speaker: Dr Chia Shi-Lu (Tanjong Pagar)
text: The Ministry has indicated that it is prepared to be flexible and may accept alternative solutions for buildings which encounter technical problems installing such features.

speaker: Dr Chia Shi-Lu (Tanjong Pagar)
text: I appeal to SCDF to adhere to its high standards.

speaker: Dr Chia Shi-Lu (Tanjong Pagar)
text: But alternatives which compromise on safety should not be permitted.

speaker: Dr Chia Shi-Lu (Tanjong Pagar)
text: I have a question regarding the evacuation of persons with mobility problems.

speaker: Dr Chia Shi-Lu (Tanjong Pagar)
text: With our rapidly ageing population and integration of persons with disabilities into our workforce, we can expect more persons with mobility issues in our workplaces as well as other buildings, including residences.

speaker: Dr Chia Shi-Lu (Tanjong Pagar)
text: What provisions do we have in the protected stairways to enable the safe evacuation of the less abled or the disabled?

speaker: Dr Chia Shi-Lu (Tanjong Pagar)
text: Fire safety products used in buildings do play a very important role and we are all aware of the examples of the Toh Guan Road industrial complex fire in May 2017 and London's Grenfell Tower inferno just one month later.

speaker: Dr Chia Shi-Lu (Tanjong Pagar)
text: The external cladding in both cases accelerated the spread of the fire.

speaker: Dr Chia Shi-Lu (Tanjong Pagar)
text: I and including others, have raised this concern in this House previously.

speaker: Dr Chia Shi-Lu (Tanjong Pagar)
text: Grenfell Tower also had similar deficiencies as the Kyoto Animation building in lacking a fire sprinkler system and having only one stairway, which the survivors later reported were blocked and full of smoke, an indication that the fire doors had failed.

speaker: Dr Chia Shi-Lu (Tanjong Pagar)
text: Such a move would enhance the fire safety of materials used in new buildings.

speaker: Dr Chia Shi-Lu (Tanjong Pagar)
text: However, in the meanwhile, what about downstream consequences?

speaker: Dr Chia Shi-Lu (Tanjong Pagar)
text: Would the Ministry consider conducting from now, spot checks and audits on existing buildings and require replacements should there be deficiencies due to less stringent fire safety standards applied in the past or perhaps because of deterioration over time?

speaker: Mr Gan Thiam Poh (Ang Mo Kio)
text: Deputy Speaker, Sir, I welcome the amendments to the Act to empower SCDF to take a wider range of actions for fire safety, in particular, the enhancement of its investigative and enforcement powers.

speaker: Mr Gan Thiam Poh (Ang Mo Kio)
text: Without regular enforcement and meaningful penalties, complacency sets in and, over time, increasing numbers of business owners and residents engage in inconsiderate and risky behaviours.

speaker: Mr Gan Thiam Poh (Ang Mo Kio)
text: These include the failure to maintain fire safety equipment or evacuation routes, allowing the overcrowding of people and goods, and using poor quality electrical devices from suppliers, or using the devices inappropriately.

speaker: Mr Gan Thiam Poh (Ang Mo Kio)
text: Most fires can be prevented but it requires the cooperation of everyone.

speaker: Mr Gan Thiam Poh (Ang Mo Kio)
text: We need more consistent public education and outreach programmes to teach and remind all residents of safe practices and installations.

speaker: Mr Gan Thiam Poh (Ang Mo Kio)
text: One of the biggest fire safety challenges in residential premises is the cluttering of passageways by plants, household items, trolleys and PMDs.

speaker: Mr Gan Thiam Poh (Ang Mo Kio)
text: I am sure all my Parliamentary colleagues have been receiving complaints about this problem.

speaker: Mr Gan Thiam Poh (Ang Mo Kio)
text: In addition, no flammable items should be kept along common corridors or in staircases.

speaker: Mr Gan Thiam Poh (Ang Mo Kio)
text: Some homeowners can be very stubborn and treat the areas outside their homes as their property.

speaker: Mr Gan Thiam Poh (Ang Mo Kio)
text: Such obstructions have been the source of inconvenience and disputes among neighbours for many years.

speaker: Mr Gan Thiam Poh (Ang Mo Kio)
text: So far, it has not been easy to resolve these problems as certain homeowners have been uncooperative and even refused to turn up for mediation.

speaker: Mr Gan Thiam Poh (Ang Mo Kio)
text: I hope the Ministry could provide tools and avenues to Town Councils and homeowners to resolve such problems expeditiously.

speaker: Mr Gan Thiam Poh (Ang Mo Kio)
text: If the inspectors spot problems in the common areas, appropriate action can be taken, with education as a priority.

speaker: Mr Gan Thiam Poh (Ang Mo Kio)
text: However, it is difficult for inspectors to detect flammable items hoarded within one's home.

speaker: Mr Gan Thiam Poh (Ang Mo Kio)
text: The behavior of these residents certainly poses a great risk to other neighbours.

speaker: Mr Gan Thiam Poh (Ang Mo Kio)
text: If these homeowners are unable to modify their behavior, would the Government consider providing them with alternative accommodation with more fire safety features?

speaker: Mr Gan Thiam Poh (Ang Mo Kio)
text: It is unfair and unsafe to subject their neighbours to such fire risks, especially when these families have young children or elderly with mobility problems.

speaker: Mr Gan Thiam Poh (Ang Mo Kio)
text: I hope these fire safety systems will become standard features in all buildings in Singapore.

speaker: Mr Melvin Yong Yik Chye (Tanjong Pagar)
text: Although the number of fire incidents has remained stable in recent years, every fire poses a significant risk to lives and properties.

speaker: Mr Melvin Yong Yik Chye (Tanjong Pagar)
text: It is, therefore, imperative that we review and update our fire safety regulations periodically.

speaker: Mr Melvin Yong Yik Chye (Tanjong Pagar)
text: While I support the Bill, I have a few questions.

speaker: Mr Melvin Yong Yik Chye (Tanjong Pagar)
text: First, I support the new provisions in the Bill to empower SCDF to mandate building owners to install fire safety critical upgrades, if deemed necessary for public safety.

speaker: Mr Melvin Yong Yik Chye (Tanjong Pagar)
text: Currently, changes to the Fire Code can only be applied prospectively to new buildings, and to existing ones that undergo A&A works.

speaker: Mr Melvin Yong Yik Chye (Tanjong Pagar)
text: But when a fire breaks out and spreads, it does not discriminate between older or newer buildings.

speaker: Mr Melvin Yong Yik Chye (Tanjong Pagar)
text: Therefore, we must ensure that occupants in all buildings are safe.

speaker: Mr Melvin Yong Yik Chye (Tanjong Pagar)
text: However, the costs involved for building owners to comply with the latest Fire Code can be significant.

speaker: Mr Melvin Yong Yik Chye (Tanjong Pagar)
text: It is likely that some of these buildings may require a substantial overhaul to comply with the latest Fire Code.

speaker: Mr Melvin Yong Yik Chye (Tanjong Pagar)
text: Will the Ministry provide assistance to these building owners to help them become compliant to the latest Fire Code?

speaker: Mr Melvin Yong Yik Chye (Tanjong Pagar)
text: Due to our ageing population, these older buildings, some of which are in my constituency, are looking at installing lifts to better serve the needs of their elderly occupants.

speaker: Mr Melvin Yong Yik Chye (Tanjong Pagar)
text: But since they have not undergone any A&A works previously, major overhauls, such as having to build an entirely new fire escape stairwell, are needed to comply with the latest Fire Code.

speaker: Mr Melvin Yong Yik Chye (Tanjong Pagar)
text: This presents the building owners with an extremely prohibitive cost, when all they want is to simply build a lift to cater to the mobility needs of their ageing occupants.

speaker: Mr Melvin Yong Yik Chye (Tanjong Pagar)
text: So, they tell me, "We cannot install the lift because, if we install the lift, we need to comply with the latest Fire Code.

speaker: Mr Melvin Yong Yik Chye (Tanjong Pagar)
text: But if we do not install the lift, then we are in compliance with the old Fire Code." Can the Ministry look into how we can help these older buildings lower the prohibitive costs of fire safety compliance when undergoing such A&A works?

speaker: Mr Melvin Yong Yik Chye (Tanjong Pagar)
text: I am sure this number has grown significantly in the 14 years since the study was concluded.

speaker: Mr Melvin Yong Yik Chye (Tanjong Pagar)
text: Allowing SCDF to outsource routine checks would, therefore, allow the agency to better optimise its resources.

speaker: Mr Melvin Yong Yik Chye (Tanjong Pagar)
text: However, outsourcing comes with the risk that poorly trained enforcement officers would tarnish the reputation of SCDF.

speaker: Mr Melvin Yong Yik Chye (Tanjong Pagar)
text: Members would have heard of various issues associated with outsourced enforcement officers.

speaker: Mr Melvin Yong Yik Chye (Tanjong Pagar)
text: Therefore, it is important that we provide these supplementary enforcement officers with the appropriate training, both in terms of technical skills and the soft skills of engaging building management and members of the public.

speaker: Mr Melvin Yong Yik Chye (Tanjong Pagar)
text: Could the Ministry, therefore, share more on the training that these supplementary enforcement officers would undergo?

speaker: Mr Melvin Yong Yik Chye (Tanjong Pagar)
text: Beyond training, another way to reduce issues associated with outsourced enforcement officers is to engage officers, individuals, who already have a wealth of relevant experience.

speaker: Mr Melvin Yong Yik Chye (Tanjong Pagar)
text: This is where the Labour Movement can come in.

speaker: Mr Melvin Yong Yik Chye (Tanjong Pagar)
text: Our unions have many members who are retired fire wardens, safety officers and facilities management officers, many of whom will be keen to return to work with some form of training.

speaker: Mr Melvin Yong Yik Chye (Tanjong Pagar)
text: I urge SCDF to work closely with our unions and engage these experienced officers as possible supplementary enforcement officers.

speaker: Mr Melvin Yong Yik Chye (Tanjong Pagar)
text: With the recent spate of PMD-related fires, it is important that we continue to educate the public on the need to ensure that their PMDs are compliant with the safety standards, and on safe charging habits.

speaker: Mr Melvin Yong Yik Chye (Tanjong Pagar)
text: While I note that SCDF has infographics about fire safety tips for PMDs and PABs on their social media channels, more work needs to be done to increase awareness, in particular, for those who are not on social media channels.

speaker: Mr Melvin Yong Yik Chye (Tanjong Pagar)
text: Perhaps, the supplementary enforcement officers could double up their roles and educate the public on proper fire safety practices, when conducting their inspections.

speaker: Mr Melvin Yong Yik Chye (Tanjong Pagar)
text: SCDF and the Land Transport Authority should also work closely with vendors of these PMDs and PABs to educate their users on the proper charging of their devices at the point of sale.

speaker: Mr Melvin Yong Yik Chye (Tanjong Pagar)
text: While education and awareness are important, they alone are insufficient.

speaker: Mr Melvin Yong Yik Chye (Tanjong Pagar)
text: I do agree with Er Dr Lee Bee Wah that with so many non-compliant PMDs in our housing estates, there is a risk of a PMD-related fire every day.

speaker: Mr Melvin Yong Yik Chye (Tanjong Pagar)
text: If so, can we focus our inspections on these devices?

speaker: Mr Melvin Yong Yik Chye (Tanjong Pagar)
text: So, while we increase the regulatory powers of SCDF as part of our periodic review of the fire safety regulations, it is important that we extend support to those impacted.

speaker: Mr Melvin Yong Yik Chye (Tanjong Pagar)
text: I urge the Ministry to do more in helping owners of older buildings to become compliant with new regulations, and to engage our unions to employ experienced officers as supplementary enforcement officers.

speaker: Ms Anthea Ong (Nominated Member)
text: However, all four fire fatalities last year took place in residential buildings.

speaker: Ms Anthea Ong (Nominated Member)
text: The majority of the 90 fire injuries attended to by SCDF last year involved fires also in residential buildings.

speaker: Ms Anthea Ong (Nominated Member)
text: I would, therefore, argue that there is also a need to update and reinforce fire safety measures in residential buildings, especially for our elderly and disability populations.

speaker: Ms Anthea Ong (Nominated Member)
text: In May this year, an 83-year-old woman who was also a wheelchair user was found dead in her Bukit Panjang flat from a fire sparked off by a lit joss stick.

speaker: Ms Anthea Ong (Nominated Member)
text: The investigation revealed that she was unlikely to have been able to evacuate on her own when the fire broke out.

speaker: Ms Anthea Ong (Nominated Member)
text: Her daughter, who had gone out to buy lunch, came back to find the flat on fire.

speaker: Ms Anthea Ong (Nominated Member)
text: Her mother, who had been diagnosed with dementia, was unable to get out of the flat, and succumbed to smoke inhalation.

speaker: Ms Anthea Ong (Nominated Member)
text: She was one of the four elderly who died in home fires between 2015 and 2017.

speaker: Ms Anthea Ong (Nominated Member)
text: A 2008 Norwegian study found that those over 70 years old are four times more vulnerable in the event of a fire.

speaker: Ms Anthea Ong (Nominated Member)
text: Indeed, the need to address fire safety issues within our built environment is all the more urgent, given that by 2030, one in four of our population will be aged 65 or older.

speaker: Ms Anthea Ong (Nominated Member)
text: By 2050, this number is projected to reach 3.08 million.

speaker: Ms Anthea Ong (Nominated Member)
text: This means that in three decades, 47% of Singapore's total population will be 65 years old or older.

speaker: Ms Anthea Ong (Nominated Member)
text: This number is expected to grow beyond 100,000 by 2030.

speaker: Ms Anthea Ong (Nominated Member)
text: How we support them with fire safety measures could make a big difference to how long they can remain independent.

speaker: Ms Anthea Ong (Nominated Member)
text: There are 103,758 in 2015, approximately 10% of the population aged 65 and above who are illiterate.

speaker: Ms Anthea Ong (Nominated Member)
text: These seniors may not understand the fire evacuation maps even if they are prominently displayed in their blocks, in the event of a fire.

speaker: Ms Anthea Ong (Nominated Member)
text: Fire safety is clearly not the responsibility of SCDF alone.

speaker: Ms Anthea Ong (Nominated Member)
text: The responsibility is one to be shared across Ministries and the community.

speaker: Ms Anthea Ong (Nominated Member)
text: Let us look upstream at some measures that can prevent fires from happening for our vulnerable communities.

speaker: Ms Anthea Ong (Nominated Member)
text: First, we should rope in our 250,000-strong foreign domestic workers (FDW) to be part of this effort because: (a) they are often caregivers to the elderly and disability populations, and children; (b) they are often at home during the day and could prove to be a valuable resource should a fire break out within the neighbourhood; and (c) they themselves are at risk in case of a fire outbreak.

speaker: Ms Anthea Ong (Nominated Member)
text: Currently, a FDW spends a few weeks being trained in their home country on the usual cleaning and caregiving skills.

speaker: Ms Anthea Ong (Nominated Member)
text: As far as fire safety training is concerned, they are merely taught to inform their employer and call the emergency hotline number in times of a fire emergency.

speaker: Ms Anthea Ong (Nominated Member)
text: Aside from regular FDWs, employers also have the option of hiring pre-trained domestic workers who have undergone comprehensive training to take care of the elderly.

speaker: Ms Anthea Ong (Nominated Member)
text: Under the Eldercare FDW Scheme, they learn to assist them in daily activities, tend to them with medication and be trained in first aid.

speaker: Ms Anthea Ong (Nominated Member)
text: Again, fire safety does not feature in the training programme.

speaker: Ms Anthea Ong (Nominated Member)
text: The Safety Guidelines for FDWs by MOM have a singular focus on window-cleaning, following several high-rise fall incidents in the past.

speaker: Ms Anthea Ong (Nominated Member)
text: Employers are also encouraged to teach these helpers how to handle electrical appliances and preventive measures, such as not touching plugs when hands are wet.

speaker: Ms Anthea Ong (Nominated Member)
text: Again, fire safety is not included in these guidelines.

speaker: Ms Anthea Ong (Nominated Member)
text: In addition, Mr Deputy Speaker, our domestic helpers are also not taught how to use a fire extinguisher or the automated emergency defibrillator (AED) or how to evacuate properly in the event of an emergency.

speaker: Ms Anthea Ong (Nominated Member)
text: Community programmes organised by SCDF, like the Community Emergency Preparedness Programmes, focus on essential emergency procedures like fire safety and evacuation procedures among first-aid programmes as well.

speaker: Ms Anthea Ong (Nominated Member)
text: We must equip them adequately so that they have the confidence to act decisively in case of fire and other emergencies which can be very valuable in saving lives, especially when caring for the young, elderly and differently-abled.

speaker: Ms Anthea Ong (Nominated Member)
text: Second, we must harness the power of the community.

speaker: Ms Anthea Ong (Nominated Member)
text: As we roll out Dementia Friendly Communities, the neighbourhood is aware of issues arising from dementia and can better support these individuals who live alone.

speaker: Ms Anthea Ong (Nominated Member)
text: The volunteers, also known as Dementia Friends, could support persons with dementia by checking in on them regularly and advising them on minimising the risk of fire hazards.

speaker: Ms Anthea Ong (Nominated Member)
text: In addition, fire safety training should also be given to the caregivers of these households, designated neighbours and these Dementia Friends.

speaker: Ms Anthea Ong (Nominated Member)
text: Assistive technologies in the home environment, such as gas shut-off valves and sprinkler systems, are preventive measures.

speaker: Ms Anthea Ong (Nominated Member)
text: While I concede that there is a significant financial consideration in installing water sprinklers in each and every household, installing sprinklers in vulnerable households where the resident does not have the ability to quell the fire on his own or evacuate quickly must be an option to be seriously considered.

speaker: Ms Anthea Ong (Nominated Member)
text: Would the elderly lady on a wheelchair I mentioned earlier in Bukit Panjang have lived if she had a sprinkler in her flat?

speaker: Ms Anthea Ong (Nominated Member)
text: Last but not least, Mr Deputy Speaker, I would like to raise the issue of smoke alarms and fire extinguishers in homes.

speaker: Ms Anthea Ong (Nominated Member)
text: Even as the national effort to install smoke detectors in all new residential flats is in place, fire extinguishers and smoke alarm installations are still only highly encouraged by SCDF, and the take-up rates remain low.

speaker: Ms Anthea Ong (Nominated Member)
text: Yet, they remain essential tools to stop small blazes from growing bigger.

speaker: Ms Anthea Ong (Nominated Member)
text: Smoke alarms decrease the probability of fatal fire incidents dramatically.

speaker: Ms Anthea Ong (Nominated Member)
text: While having a mandatory fire extinguisher policy is believed to be difficult because of financial costs, a risk-based approach is needed.

speaker: Ms Anthea Ong (Nominated Member)
text: As shared earlier, fires happen more often than we think, Mr Deputy Speaker, especially in residential homes.

speaker: Ms Anthea Ong (Nominated Member)
text: And when they do, the cost of a fire extinguisher pales in comparison to the material and psychological damage caused.

speaker: Ms Anthea Ong (Nominated Member)
text: One of my team members shared this story with me as I was writing this speech.

speaker: Ms Anthea Ong (Nominated Member)
text: Almost a year ago, he was woken up in the middle of the night by his neighbour whose flat had caught fire from an electrical short circuit.

speaker: Ms Anthea Ong (Nominated Member)
text: The neighbour, despite being in a crisis himself, made sure that his daughter alerted the neighbours to leave their homes in case the fire spreads.

speaker: Ms Anthea Ong (Nominated Member)
text: The swift response by SCDF ensured that everything was soon under control.

speaker: Ms Anthea Ong (Nominated Member)
text: This neighbour and his family were not allowed to go back into their home until the investigations were over.

speaker: Ms Anthea Ong (Nominated Member)
text: Besides, smoke had spread throughout the flat making it unsafe to occupy.

speaker: Ms Anthea Ong (Nominated Member)
text: For a few hours, this neighbour and his family were able to rest in my team member’s flat to clean up and compose themselves before their friends came to take them in for the night, and then weeks after.

speaker: Ms Anthea Ong (Nominated Member)
text: SCDF conducted various examinations to determine the origin and cause of fire, the Police conducted their on-scene investigations, and the insurance company surveyed and assessed the fire damage.

speaker: Ms Anthea Ong (Nominated Member)
text: The neighbours engaged companies for the repair and restoration works, including clearing the soot from the smoke, rewiring of the house and painting.

speaker: Ms Anthea Ong (Nominated Member)
text: During the ordeal, the neighbour and his family felt like "refugees" for those few weeks when they had to seek refuge with their friends.

speaker: Ms Anthea Ong (Nominated Member)
text: Yet the burning question in my mind when he shared the story was: did his neighbour have a fire extinguisher in his flat?

speaker: Ms Anthea Ong (Nominated Member)
text: The blaze was so small when it first started from the electric wire, an extinguisher would have quelled it in seconds and the trauma and anguish of many weeks could have been averted.

speaker: Ms Anthea Ong (Nominated Member)
text: Can we offer schemes to subsidise such installations as mandatory for vulnerable households alongside the fire safety training I mentioned earlier?

speaker: Ms Anthea Ong (Nominated Member)
text: How do we make sure that the elderly and persons with disabilities or those with mobility difficulties are provided safe evacuation routes in the event of a fire?

speaker: Ms Anthea Ong (Nominated Member)
text: How can the deaf or hard of hearing become cognisant of a fire if they cannot hear smoke alarms?

speaker: Ms Anthea Ong (Nominated Member)
text: How can persons with mobility difficulties be evacuated off a high-rise building if lifts are not to be used and they are unable to take the stairs?

speaker: Ms Anthea Ong (Nominated Member)
text: What more can we do for persons with dementia at home?

speaker: Ms Anthea Ong (Nominated Member)
text: We may not always have the right answers, but we must not stop asking the right questions.

speaker: Ms Anthea Ong (Nominated Member)
text: For that is the only way for us to fireproof our future as a caring and inclusive society.

speaker: Ms Anthea Ong (Nominated Member)
text: At this juncture, I would also like to join my fellow Members to thank the SCDF for the work they do for the country.

speaker: Mr Patrick Tay Teck Guan (West Coast)
text: In the last two weeks, I witnessed three fires happening in my Boon Lay constituency.

speaker: Mr Patrick Tay Teck Guan (West Coast)
text: One at a rental flat, another at the void deck and one at a commercial shop premises.

speaker: Mr Patrick Tay Teck Guan (West Coast)
text: In particular, the offences mainly involve the unauthorised change of use of premises which could cause existing fire safety measures to become inadequate, as well as instances where industry professionals, such as registered inspectors, do not responsibly supervise and certify fire safety work.

speaker: Mr Patrick Tay Teck Guan (West Coast)
text: The penalty for the failure of an appointed Qualified Person to supervise fire safety work will also be raised.

speaker: Mr Patrick Tay Teck Guan (West Coast)
text: Updating and raising these penalties will help address upstream the causes of fires and mitigate if not eradicate fires in built up areas.

speaker: Mr Patrick Tay Teck Guan (West Coast)
text: At present, when dealing with fire hazards, SCDF must first issue a Fire Hazard Abatement Notice and can only act against the errant parties if they fail to comply with the Notice.

speaker: Mr Patrick Tay Teck Guan (West Coast)
text: However, some fire hazards may pose "serious and significant" fire safety risks and, where time is of the essence, to nip the problem in the bud.

speaker: Mr Patrick Tay Teck Guan (West Coast)
text: Its officers will then be able to investigate suspects for fire safety violations and take statements when there is reasonable suspicion of an offence.

speaker: Mr Patrick Tay Teck Guan (West Coast)
text: Notwithstanding, I have two incendiary concerns and will provide suggestions to these two areas.

speaker: Mr Patrick Tay Teck Guan (West Coast)
text: First, I am particularly concerned about the types, accessibility and sale of fire extinguishers.

speaker: Mr Patrick Tay Teck Guan (West Coast)
text: Can MHA share more about the roles and responsibilities of the different supply chain actors, how the new measures will improve fire safety, and the cost implication of these measures to the industry and to building owners?

speaker: Mr Patrick Tay Teck Guan (West Coast)
text: How about unregulated fire safety products and the control over them?

speaker: Mr Patrick Tay Teck Guan (West Coast)
text: In the same vein, how can the general public and consumer best verify the right type of fire extinguisher to procure and use for their homes, premises and offices and whether there is a way to validate the authenticity and efficacy of these products?

speaker: Mr Patrick Tay Teck Guan (West Coast)
text: In short, for the layman, how to know what type to buy, which size for their premises, from where and whom they should be purchasing the fire extinguishers and fire safety devices and products from.

speaker: Mr Patrick Tay Teck Guan (West Coast)
text: Second, with increased adoption and installation of smart homes and more people having their own devices to detect smoke, burning and fires, can SCDF make it easier for personal home alarms to be linked to a central community system or even SCDF with the caveat that users have to pay if there is a false alarm or activation where resources are sent to respond to the activated alarm?

speaker: Ms Jessica Tan Soon Neo (East Coast)
text: In densely populated Singapore and with the large number of buildings, especially high-rise buildings, ensuring fire safety of buildings is key to protecting lives in the unfortunate event of a fire.

speaker: Ms Jessica Tan Soon Neo (East Coast)
text: Crucial aspects of a building’s safety are the possibility of safe escape and compartmentalisation.

speaker: Ms Jessica Tan Soon Neo (East Coast)
text: The condition of the building will also have an impact on the speed a fire spreads or whether it is contained.

speaker: Ms Jessica Tan Soon Neo (East Coast)
text: Although this is an extreme example, the tragic fire at Grenfell Tower in the UK in 2017 is a sad case that demonstrates what could happen when all fire safety regulations of the building failed.

speaker: Ms Jessica Tan Soon Neo (East Coast)
text: From the cladding of the building, the quality of the renovations, outstanding fire safety issues, all these were a combination of factors that led to the disastrous consequences and the unnecessary loss of many lives.

speaker: Ms Jessica Tan Soon Neo (East Coast)
text: While I am supportive of the Bill, I do have some feedback and clarifications.

speaker: Ms Jessica Tan Soon Neo (East Coast)
text: While we all agree that safety cannot be compromised, the stricter requirements will increase construction schedules and the cost will affect both the building owners and tenants.

speaker: Ms Jessica Tan Soon Neo (East Coast)
text: As fire safety experts, SCDF is best positioned and must take a practical approach to work with building owners to comply with the safety standards while managing costs.

speaker: Ms Jessica Tan Soon Neo (East Coast)
text: Ensuring that buildings meet fire safety regulation standards is important.

speaker: Ms Jessica Tan Soon Neo (East Coast)
text: But equally critical is the building's fire detection and alarm system, evacuation plans and policy in the event of a fire.

speaker: Ms Jessica Tan Soon Neo (East Coast)
text: As the Bill will empower SCDF to investigate fire hazards and to mandate building owners to comply with fire safety regulations, how does SCDF ensure that buildings have in place appropriate building fire evacuation plans and policies?

speaker: Ms Jessica Tan Soon Neo (East Coast)
text: This is as crucial as the physical infrastructure and fire regulations of the building.

speaker: Ms Jessica Tan Soon Neo (East Coast)
text: This will allow SCDF officers to focus on more complex enforcement.

speaker: Ms Jessica Tan Soon Neo (East Coast)
text: While the tasks of building inspections and fire safety enforcement checks are routine, they do require SCDF officers to be on the ground.

speaker: Ms Jessica Tan Soon Neo (East Coast)
text: This will give them a good feel and assessment of the fire safety conditions of buildings.

speaker: Ms Jessica Tan Soon Neo (East Coast)
text: By outsourcing these tasks to authorised third parties, I do hope that there will be a balance of using authorised third parties for these tasks and still have SCDF officers stay connected with the ground conditions and, more importantly, the insights of what is happening on the ground.

speaker: Ms Jessica Tan Soon Neo (East Coast)
text: While the tasks of conducting inspections and enforcements are routine, they are also important tasks to ensure that the buildings meet the fire safety standards.

speaker: Ms Jessica Tan Soon Neo (East Coast)
text: To this point, how will SCDF ensure the quality of the tasks done by the authorised third parties?

speaker: Ms Jessica Tan Soon Neo (East Coast)
text: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary did share that there would be measures to safeguard the quality of these parties, and these include audits as well as body-worn cameras.

speaker: Ms Jessica Tan Soon Neo (East Coast)
text: Can more details be provided in terms of the benchmarks, criteria and the frequency of such audits?

speaker: Ms Jessica Tan Soon Neo (East Coast)
text: I do want to take the opportunity to also thank our SCDF officers for the work that they do and for keeping Singaporeans safe.

speaker: Ms Jessica Tan Soon Neo (East Coast)
text: To protect lives, it is essential that fire safety regulations stay relevant and that there is continued maintenance and testing of fire safety standards and inspection to ensure our buildings are fire-safe.

speaker: Ms Irene Quay Siew Ching (Nominated Member)
text: MHA should be commended for their progressive and pre-emptive responses to install fire alarm devices, or smoke detectors in short, for new and existing residential premises carrying out fire safety works from 1 June 2018.

speaker: Ms Irene Quay Siew Ching (Nominated Member)
text: I understand that there are also ongoing efforts by grassroots leaders and Members of Parliament to educate residents on fire safety in their homes.

speaker: Ms Irene Quay Siew Ching (Nominated Member)
text: It is, therefore, very regrettable that MHA is not insisting for smoke detector HFADs to be installed in all existing residential premises that are not carrying out fire safety works.

speaker: Ms Irene Quay Siew Ching (Nominated Member)
text: This is in spite of the fact that existing homeowners are strongly encouraged to install smoke detectors for their own safety.

speaker: Ms Irene Quay Siew Ching (Nominated Member)
text: Consequently, I would like to ask MHA the reasons for the differing treatment and if there are any long-term plans to make smoke detector installations mandatory for existing residential premises?

speaker: Ms Irene Quay Siew Ching (Nominated Member)
text: In 2017, the President of the Fire Safety Managers' Association forewarned that "in many cases of home fires, there have been cases of injuries or death due to smoke inhalation, which could have happened while the occupants were asleep.

speaker: Ms Irene Quay Siew Ching (Nominated Member)
text: A localised smoke alarm will alert residents so that they can react to the fire at an early stage." He also cautioned that the voluntary take-up rate of fire alarms and extinguishers in homes has been low, despite encouragement from the authorities.

speaker: Ms Irene Quay Siew Ching (Nominated Member)
text: A fire safety expert from a fire safety solutions provider in Singapore clarified that often, the deadliest fires are small fires that quietly smoulder and cause smoke while people are sleeping or are in a different room.

speaker: Ms Irene Quay Siew Ching (Nominated Member)
text: Without the early warning provided by an alarm, people can be overcome by smoke even before the fire is discovered.

speaker: Ms Irene Quay Siew Ching (Nominated Member)
text: A 2015 report by the US National Fire Protection Association has found that the fatality rate from residential fires in homes with working alarms was 40% lower than in those without.

speaker: Ms Irene Quay Siew Ching (Nominated Member)
text: The predominant reasons cited by SCDF for residential fires were materials set alight in rubbish chutes, bins or unattended cooking.

speaker: Ms Irene Quay Siew Ching (Nominated Member)
text: Recently, we have observed an increase in PMD-related fire incidents.

speaker: Ms Irene Quay Siew Ching (Nominated Member)
text: As we can see from the statistics I have cited, smoke detectors would be very effective as a preventive fire safety measure, as they would provide residents with an early warning sign.

speaker: Ms Irene Quay Siew Ching (Nominated Member)
text: So, my proposition to improve fire safety for all residential areas are twofold.

speaker: Ms Irene Quay Siew Ching (Nominated Member)
text: A short-term plan would be for SCDF to introduce a fire safety checklist to raise awareness and the level of fire safety standards in homes.

speaker: Ms Irene Quay Siew Ching (Nominated Member)
text: Furthermore, the Government should ramp up educational efforts in the community and in shared spaces on fire safety.

speaker: Ms Irene Quay Siew Ching (Nominated Member)
text: Perhaps, volunteers from the neighbourhood watch zone or Silver Generation Ambassadors can be engaged to expedite efforts to encourage the take-up of fire extinguisher or smoke detectors.

speaker: Ms Irene Quay Siew Ching (Nominated Member)
text: Consequently, certified smoke detectors, fire extinguishers or fire blankets should be made more accessible and affordable within the community for purchase as they are the first lines of defence in the event of fire.

speaker: Ms Irene Quay Siew Ching (Nominated Member)
text: For this purpose, a national procurement competition would be very suited to design and introduce a lightweight and all-purpose fire extinguisher easily used by the young and elderly.

speaker: Ms Irene Quay Siew Ching (Nominated Member)
text: Residents may not be aware that water cannot put out grease fire, and also, fire extinguishers are loaded with different dousing agents to fight specific fires.

speaker: Ms Irene Quay Siew Ching (Nominated Member)
text: Some extinguishers are ineffective against certain fires, while others could potentially worsen the situation.

speaker: Ms Irene Quay Siew Ching (Nominated Member)
text: Having an easy to use and lightweight all-purpose extinguisher at hand will infinitely reduce the threat of a fire emergency.

speaker: Ms Irene Quay Siew Ching (Nominated Member)
text: Supermarkets can then be involved with the sale of this extinguisher to make it more accessible.

speaker: Ms Irene Quay Siew Ching (Nominated Member)
text: This way, residents will not need to worry if the fire extinguisher they purchase is certified, as there are many types of uncertified extinguishers available online.

speaker: Ms Irene Quay Siew Ching (Nominated Member)
text: I then move on to ask if the revised Act will cover online sales of non-certified fire extinguishers and how do the authorities plan to regulate this?

speaker: Ms Irene Quay Siew Ching (Nominated Member)
text: To continue with my proposition, a long-term plan would involve the execution of a five- to 10-year phase which will introduce new legislation, in view of increasing fire risks from an ageing population and from more extensive use of PMDs.

speaker: Ms Irene Quay Siew Ching (Nominated Member)
text: The implementation process may be long, but we need to start with the first step.

speaker: Ms Irene Quay Siew Ching (Nominated Member)
text: This new legislation shall include mandatory installation of fire alarms, both exterior along HDB corridors and interior in homes, while concurrently equipping all homes with a fire extinguisher or at least a fire blanket for economical reasons or practical maintenance.

speaker: Ms Irene Quay Siew Ching (Nominated Member)
text: I hope my suggestions provide much needed insight and I look forward to having them considered seriously and implemented.

speaker: Ms Joan Pereira (Tanjong Pagar)
text: It is important to review our fire safety legislation periodically to ensure that it remains effective in the face of changes in our environment and user behaviour.

speaker: Ms Joan Pereira (Tanjong Pagar)
text: Our older HDB flats are fitted with individual rubbish chutes, which are quite different from the new flats where residents have to dispose of their rubbish through central chute systems.

speaker: Ms Joan Pereira (Tanjong Pagar)
text: Central chutes are equipped with sprinkler systems to douse fires.

speaker: Ms Joan Pereira (Tanjong Pagar)
text: However, the older individual chutes do not have these sprinklers.

speaker: Ms Joan Pereira (Tanjong Pagar)
text: Does the Ministry have alternative safety measures to address this problem?

speaker: Ms Joan Pereira (Tanjong Pagar)
text: (In Mandarin):   The Bill seeks to enhance the fire safety of buildings by empowering SCDF to require building owners to install critical fire safety features, such as protected exit staircases and fire alarm systems.

speaker: Ms Joan Pereira (Tanjong Pagar)
text: Every year, over 2,000 fires break out in residences, with about half being rubbish chute fires.

speaker: Ms Joan Pereira (Tanjong Pagar)
text: Our older HDB flats are fitted with individual rubbish chutes, which are quite different from the new flats where residents have to dispose of their rubbish through central chute systems.

speaker: Ms Joan Pereira (Tanjong Pagar)
text: Central chutes are equipped with sprinklers to douse fires.

speaker: Ms Joan Pereira (Tanjong Pagar)
text: However, the older individual chutes do not have these sprinklers.

speaker: Ms Joan Pereira (Tanjong Pagar)
text: Does the Ministry have alternative safety measures to address this problem?

speaker: Ms Joan Pereira (Tanjong Pagar)
text: (In English): Furthermore, we have a higher proportion of elderly Singaporeans living in such older HDB blocks.

speaker: Ms Joan Pereira (Tanjong Pagar)
text: This is of great concern as they are less mobile, probably less alert and less sensitive to changes in ambient temperatures and the presence of smoke.

speaker: Ms Joan Pereira (Tanjong Pagar)
text: Therefore, they may be slower to detect fire threats.

speaker: Ms Joan Pereira (Tanjong Pagar)
text: However, this still leaves the majority of residences, both HDB flats and private properties, not equipped with fire alarm systems, although owners are strongly encouraged to install them.

speaker: Ms Joan Pereira (Tanjong Pagar)
text: Does the Ministry have data on the percentage of homes installed with such devices?

speaker: Ms Joan Pereira (Tanjong Pagar)
text: Does SCDF have a list of approved HFADs and their suppliers for homeowners' reference?

speaker: Ms Joan Pereira (Tanjong Pagar)
text: This is important, as poor-quality devices can lead to a false sense of security, which can be dangerous, or create false alarms.

speaker: Ms Joan Pereira (Tanjong Pagar)
text: Another challenge is dealing with fires in very tall buildings.

speaker: Ms Joan Pereira (Tanjong Pagar)
text: The average height of our buildings has been increasing.

speaker: Ms Joan Pereira (Tanjong Pagar)
text: It is very common now for our HDB blocks and condominiums to be over 40 storeys high.

speaker: Ms Joan Pereira (Tanjong Pagar)
text: How prepared are we to deal with fires in such tall buildings, especially the elderly with mobility challenges?

speaker: Ms Joan Pereira (Tanjong Pagar)
text: Can SCDF work with our grassroots organisations on fire drills and evacuation paths in our HDB and private estates?

speaker: Ms Joan Pereira (Tanjong Pagar)
text: Would the Ministry share how successful SCDF has been in public education efforts and reaching out to our residents to increase their awareness of fire safety?

speaker: Ms Joan Pereira (Tanjong Pagar)
text: While they can be bought online, if SCDF could work with supermarket chains, such as National Trades Union Congress (NTUC) FairPrice, to sell fire extinguishers, they would be more readily accessible, especially to the elderly, many of whom do not shop online.

speaker: Ms Joan Pereira (Tanjong Pagar)
text: In addition, the physical presence of fire extinguishers in these supermarkets would be a constant reminder to all customers of the need for fire safety.

speaker: Ms Joan Pereira (Tanjong Pagar)
text: I hope the Ministry would consider this suggestion.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Home Affairs (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: Members have raised many pertinent points on the importance of enhancing the fire safety of buildings and strengthening SCDF’s regulatory and enforcement powers to ensure that the fire safety regime continues to stay robust and effective for a safer Singapore.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Home Affairs (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: I will first respond to the comments pertaining to the amendments to the Fire Safety Act, namely: (a) tighter regulatory control over the supply chain for regulated fire safety products; (b) appointment of third-party officers; and (c) fire safety at public and industrial buildings.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Home Affairs (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: I will then discuss the various suggestions Members have made with regard to broader issues relating to fire safety.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Home Affairs (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: First, on the topic of tightening regulatory control over the supply chain of regulated fire safety products.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Home Affairs (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: Mr Patrick Tay and Mr Christopher de Souza asked about the roles and responsibilities of the supply chain actors and whether the tighter control would increase costs to the industry and building owners.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Home Affairs (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: I had earlier spoken on who the supply chain actors are and their respective roles.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Home Affairs (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: SCDF has consulted the affected stakeholders and has worked with them to ensure that the due diligence actions required of them are reasonable and practicable.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Home Affairs (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: In our view, these actions are not onerous and ought to be done even without the amendments to the Fire Safety Act.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Home Affairs (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: For example, certification bodies that certify regulated fire safety products should independently check the validity of the test reports submitted by the suppliers before issuing any Certificate of Conformity (CoC).

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Home Affairs (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: The amendments serve to crystallise these responsibilities in law and to allow SCDF to take non-compliant parties to task.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Home Affairs (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: Dr Chia Shi-Lu asked about the audit regime for buildings.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Home Affairs (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: SCDF regularly audits and inspects buildings to check that their fire protection systems are in proper working order.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Home Affairs (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: If the systems are faulty, SCDF will not renew the building’s Fire Certificate and the building cannot continue to be occupied.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Home Affairs (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: Mr Christopher de Souza also asked if we are enhancing the standards on the processes involving regulated fire safety products.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Home Affairs (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: This ensures that the cladding panels installed at each building are compliant.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Home Affairs (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: On this note, I will also address Ms Sylvia Lim’s question on how SCDF had assisted the building owners who were required to rectify the non-compliant claddings arising from the Toh Guan fire.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Home Affairs (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: SCDF had worked closely with them in their planning for the rectification works and ensured that, in the interim, fire safety is not compromised.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Home Affairs (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: Some building owners requested for more time to complete their rectifications.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Home Affairs (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: Where possible, SCDF had accommodated but imposed conditions, such as more frequent fire safety checks, to ensure that their fire protection systems are in working order.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Home Affairs (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: Arising from the Toh Guan fire case, other than the cases I have just mentioned, there are no other cases ongoing at the moment.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Home Affairs (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: Several Members spoke about the appointment of third-party officers to carry out enforcement tasks on behalf of SCDF.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Home Affairs (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: While most support the move to outsource these tasks, some questions were raised on the selection and training of these third-party officers, as well as the safeguards to prevent potential abuses of power and misbehaviours.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Home Affairs (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: This move is intended to allow SCDF to focus its limited resources on higher risk areas, so as to bring about better overall fire safety outcomes.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Home Affairs (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: While some inspections and enforcement tasks may be outsourced, I would like to assure Members that SCDF will maintain strong oversight over the work done by these appointed third-party officers.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Home Affairs (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: First, only simple checks will be outsourced, such as checking for any obstruction to escape routes and that emergency lights are in working order.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Home Affairs (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: At the onset, these third-party officers will only be able to exercise powers limited to evidence collection and in straightforward cases, such as obstructions of fire escape routes, empowered to make enforcement decisions, including the issuance of fire hazard abatement notices.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Home Affairs (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: Second, the third-party officers will be selected carefully.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Home Affairs (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: SCDF will specify the skills and expertise required and consider past experience in public regulatory and enforcement work favourably.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Home Affairs (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: I note Mr Melvin Yong’s point on the availability of experienced officers in the Labour Movement, and SCDF can certainly consider them.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Home Affairs (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: SCDF will also conduct training for the third-party vendor and will also be responsible for setting and administering the assessment of these officers.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Home Affairs (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: Only officers who meet SCDF’s requirements will be appointed.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Home Affairs (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: Third, we have in place safeguards against potential misbehaviours.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Home Affairs (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: The appointed third-party officers will be required to don SCDF-approved uniforms and to display SCDF-issued authority cards while on duty.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Home Affairs (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: Similar to outsourced inspection officers from the National Environment Agency, LTA and MOM, they will also be required to use body-worn cameras when on duty.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Home Affairs (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: The cameras will allow SCDF to investigate any allegations of misbehaviour.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Home Affairs (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: To Mr Louis Ng’s question on a reporting mechanism for these officers, SCDF will require them to report to SCDF Headquarters at the start and the end of their duty, to ensure that they are in proper bearing and to check that they have performed their duties properly.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Home Affairs (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: Er Dr Lee Bee Wah asked about audits.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Home Affairs (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: SCDF will conduct random audit checks on these appointed third-party officers to ensure that they are professional in their discharge of duties.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Home Affairs (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: In addition, the appointed third-party officers will be deemed as "public servants" for the purposes of the Penal Code.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Home Affairs (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: They will be expected to perform at the standards required of all public servants and be held similarly liable for breaching their public duties.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Home Affairs (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: Any person who has been issued with an enforcement notice may appeal to SCDF.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Home Affairs (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: Upon review, if the decision made by the third-party officer is assessed to be wrong, SCDF may modify or withdraw the enforcement action that has been made.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Home Affairs (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: We appreciate the timely reminder from Ms Jessica Tan and Ms Sylvia Lim that we need to strike a balance between outsourcing simple enforcement tasks to appointed third-party officers and still having SCDF officers stay connected with the ground conditions and insights.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Home Affairs (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: We will ensure that our officers continue to walk the ground and keep a finger on the pulse of the situation.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Home Affairs (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: I will now address the comments relating to the proposed power for SCDF to require building owners to install fire safety measures.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Home Affairs (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: Several Members spoke about the need to balance between ensuring fire safety standards of the buildings and taking a practical approach to help building owners manage the costs.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Home Affairs (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: As mentioned in my earlier speech, we are acutely aware of the cost implications on building owners.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Home Affairs (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: SCDF will adopt a calibrated and risk-based approach in identifying buildings for mandatory fire safety upgrades.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Home Affairs (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: To answer Ms Sylvia Lim’s question, SCDF has limited these upgrades to buildings that have higher fire safety risks, based on factors, such as the age of the building, its size, as well as the occupant load and profile.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Home Affairs (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: Even within this group, building owners will not have to undertake the full suite of upgrades to meet the prevailing Fire Code requirements, but only install selected critical fire safety measures.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Home Affairs (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: For example, only healthcare institutions will be required to have at least two compartmented rooms on each floor, as highlighted by Dr Chia Shi-Lu.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Home Affairs (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: Healthcare institutions have a high concentration of persons with mobility issues, complicating the safe evacuation of all persons out of the building during a fire.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Home Affairs (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: These compartmented rooms can serve as safe shelters for those who are unable to evacuate out of the building while awaiting the arrival of help.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Home Affairs (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: We recognise that persons with disabilities and the elderly may also be present at commercial buildings, but they are usually not in high concentration and can be evacuated out of the building with the help of other able-bodied persons.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Home Affairs (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: Furthermore, these buildings are equipped with fire lifts, which can be used to evacuate persons with mobility issues.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Home Affairs (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: Requiring the installation of compartmented rooms in these other buildings may, therefore, impose unnecessary costs on the building owners.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Home Affairs (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: Er Dr Lee Bee Wah, Mr Melvin Yong and Mr Christopher de Souza asked how SCDF will help building owners with these upgrades and how much time will be given for them to comply with the requirements.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Home Affairs (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: We are mindful that these are occupied buildings and the costs involved can be high if the upgrades required are extensive.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Home Affairs (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: We are also conscious of the fact that there may be constraints, such as costs and site limitations, when carrying out upgrading works.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Home Affairs (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: For example, building owners may engage a fire safety engineer to propose alternative solutions to address fire safety risks.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Home Affairs (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: To mitigate the risks in the interim, building owners may be required to undertake other measures, such as conducting more fire drills.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Home Affairs (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: Dr Chia Shi-Lu spoke of the need to ensure fire safety of buildings and appealed to SCDF to adhere to its high standards.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Home Affairs (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: Indeed, the public’s safety is not something we will take lightly.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Home Affairs (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: As much as SCDF wants to be flexible and accommodating to the building owners, we assure Members that SCDF scrutinises all proposals and alternative solutions carefully to ensure that fire safety standards are maintained.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Home Affairs (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: Ms Joan Pereira asked whether this new power will be used to address the problem of rubbish chute fires.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Home Affairs (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: Rubbish chute fires are typically minor and, given the enclosed area where the fire is, have less risk of spreading and a lower threat to human life.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Home Affairs (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: We will continue to educate members of the public on how to avoid and put out such fires and we will take action against culprits that cause them.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Home Affairs (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: Ms Jessica Tan has rightly pointed out that other than the requisite fire safety measures for all buildings, it is also necessary for building owners to be prepared to deal with fire emergencies, such as having fire evacuation plans.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Home Affairs (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: That is why SCDF requires public buildings to put in place certain Emergency Preparedness measures to ensure a high level of readiness amongst the occupants to respond and evacuate in the event of a fire.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Home Affairs (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: The measures include an emergency response plan that serves as a contingency plan for fire emergencies, such as an evacuation plan and the appointment of a fire safety manager to help building owners ensure a fire-safe environment.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Home Affairs (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: This means that the overcrowding of these buildings, such as places of worship and schools, will constitute a fire hazard and SCDF is empowered to take action to rectify the situation.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Home Affairs (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: The definition will also make it clear that even if a building is open to only a specific group of people, it will still be deemed a public building.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Home Affairs (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: We have engaged the building owners who are affected by this amendment, and notification letters will be sent after the new law kicks in.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Home Affairs (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: We will also work closely with the building owners to implement these measures for the safety of the occupants.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Home Affairs (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: Members have provided several suggestions on improving the fire safety of residential premises, including the installation of sprinkler systems, fire-rated doors, smoke detectors and central fire alarm systems.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Home Affairs (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: Indeed, these are useful fire safety measures that can help prevent the spread of fires or enable early evacuation of residents.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Home Affairs (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: MHA and SCDF have considered similar measures in the past and deliberated deeply on the necessity of these measures in the context of our residences.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Home Affairs (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: Residential premises have a lower occupancy load, compared to industrial and public buildings.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Home Affairs (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: And each residential unit is designed as a fire compartment to prevent the spread of fire.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Home Affairs (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: Also, residents are more familiar with the layout of the place, fire escape routes are more direct and are designed to have adequate ventilation.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Home Affairs (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: Over the years, additional infrastructure, such as rising mains and hosereels, have also been installed to aid fire-fighting operations, too.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Home Affairs (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: At this point, I would like to reiterate the fire statistics.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Home Affairs (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: The concerns that Members have raised regarding the recent increase in number of fires are due to one particular source, that is, PMDs.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Home Affairs (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: The Senior Minister of State for Transport has, in the Ministerial Statement, shared how MOT intends to address the fire safety risks of PMDs, through measures like bringing forward the deadline for compliance with the UL-2272 standard to 1 July 2020 and the introduction of a mandatory inspection regime for registered e-scooters.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Home Affairs (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: The authorities will also strengthen educational campaigns and outreach programmes on safe charging practices to enhance fire safety at home.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Home Affairs (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: We need to nip the problem in the bud to stop the fires at its source.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Home Affairs (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: And we thus have to strictly regulate PMDs and their usage so as to minimise fire hazards.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Home Affairs (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: That said, MHA and SCDF will continue to evaluate the risk environment, including taking into account our ageing population.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Home Affairs (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: We will work with building owners, including HDB, to assess the necessity to put in place additional measures that Members have suggested, such as sprinkler systems, refuge floors for lower rise HDB flats, mandatory smoke detectors and mandatory fire-rated doors, regardless of whether internal or external corridor-facing.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Home Affairs (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: We will also keep in mind the potential cost impact on homeowners, should we decide to mandate these requirements, which will require every household to install mandatory fixtures.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Home Affairs (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: Households which do not currently have smoke detectors or which do not currently require fire-rated doors can decide to purchase one on their own, for their peace of mind.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Home Affairs (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: Several Members asked why HFADs are not mandatory for all existing homes and also suggested for HFADs to be connected to a central fire alarm system.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Home Affairs (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: Assoc Prof Walter Theseira also spoke about providing support to ensure that private residences have them as well.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Home Affairs (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: The purpose of having a HFAD within a residential unit is to provide early warning to the occupants inside the house in the event of a fire, so that they can quickly extinguish the fire or evacuate to safety.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Home Affairs (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: While there may be some benefits to having HFADs linked to a central fire alarm system to provide early warning to the other residents, there are also downsides that I think Members should also be made aware of.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Home Affairs (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: Given the prevalence of smoke in our daily lives, such as from cooking or fogging activities, HFADs may give off false alarms.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Home Affairs (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: If many HFADs are connected to a central fire alarm system, the high frequency of false alarms may cause undue stress and disturbance to the residents.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Home Affairs (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: We have considered Mr Patrick Tay's suggestion of imposing charges on homeowners for false alarms.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Home Affairs (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: While it may encourage greater care from the homeowners to minimise false alarms, it may also drive other forms of behaviours, such as disconnecting the HFAD from the central fire alarm system, or to completely remove them, so as to avoid false alarms.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Home Affairs (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: This will then defeat the purpose of having HFADs in the first place.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Home Affairs (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: So, a balanced approach has to be taken.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Home Affairs (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: False alarms could be due to reasons, such as non-maintenance of the central fire alarm system, failure of the building owner to request for the alarm system to be temporarily disconnected before engaging in fogging activities, or just simply prank actions by some ill-intentioned persons.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Home Affairs (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: While we are not mandating that all existing home owners install HFADS in their homes at this point, we strongly encourage our residents to do so.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Home Affairs (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: To Ms Joan Pereira's question on whether there is a list of approved HFADs, we do not endorse any particular model, but we recommend that homeowners purchase HFADs with built-in batteries that can last up to 10 years.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Home Affairs (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: Some of these HFAD suppliers are listed on SCDF's website.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Home Affairs (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: As Ms Irene Quay had highlighted, to support the needy, SCDF is working with HDB and the People's Association to install HFADs for existing flats under the Public Rental Scheme for free.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Home Affairs (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: We will continue to encourage eligible households to come on board this scheme.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Home Affairs (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: Ms Anthea Ong had also pointed out that households with hearing-impaired occupants will not be alerted by the typical HFADs which give off an audio alarm.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Home Affairs (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: MHA will also study the need to expand the assistance scheme to broader groups of families and will work with relevant stakeholders to do so.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Home Affairs (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: Some Members also commented on the need for fire extinguishers, fire blankets and certified smoke detectors to be made more accessible and affordable and proposed for these to be equipped in all homes.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Home Affairs (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: While these are not mandatory, we strongly recommend for homeowners to have them at home.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Home Affairs (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: Fire extinguishers, for instance, can be purchased at hardware shops in the malls.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Home Affairs (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: To Mr Patrick Tay's question on how the general public can ensure that they are purchasing the right type of extinguisher for their needs, SCDF's website currently includes material on the types of extinguishers and a link to a list of companies registered to perform servicing and maintenance of fire extinguishers.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Home Affairs (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: Ms Irene Quay also suggested for a fire safety checklist to be considered for homes.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Home Affairs (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: Mr Gan Thiam Poh spoke about the fire safety risks arising from hoarding and cluttering of common areas at residential premises.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Home Affairs (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: Assoc Prof Daniel Goh also raised this point, in light of our ageing population.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Home Affairs (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: SCDF works closely with HDB and the Town Councils to address these problems.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Home Affairs (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: When SCDF receives feedback on hoarding in homes or the presence of cluttering which may constitute a fire hazard, SCDF will notify HDB or the relevant Town Council and will work with them to rectify the situation as soon as possible.
